DLSS5NVIDIA / DLSS 5 benchmark evidence center

Source-led independent guide

DLSS 5 benchmark evidence center

A useful benchmark page starts by naming the measurement. This page has not run a frame-rate test in any game; this site has no DLSS 5 game runtime. This center separates vendor-published specifications from our own image-pipeline timing and leaves unsupported frame-rate claims blank.

An evidence center for DLSS 5 claims: NVIDIA-published facts, our measured image pipeline snapshot, reproducible fields, and limits on what we can conclude.

What we have measured

One Studio batch snapshot: a 3-second 720p public-domain clip, 36 frames, an RTX 4090 reference machine, 87.4 seconds (2.43 seconds per frame), recorded on 2026-09-25; batch processing time, not real-time performance.

What we have not measured

Frame rates in any game; in-game DLSS 5 versus DLSS 4.5 comparisons; DLSS 5 performance on RTX 40 / 30 / 20 Series; any multiplier conclusions.

What cannot be inferred

NVIDIA’s up to 1.4X statement is scoped to NBA 2K27 + RTX 50 Series + RTX Spark laptops + GeForce NOW; its 10X, −24% and −20% statements also have specific scopes, are not our observations, and cannot predict other games or GPUs.

Why a single number is not a universal benchmark

DLSS 5 is a game-rendering technology with engine, driver, GPU and game-build dependencies. An image conversion pipeline has a different input, model path and output contract. Putting those numbers in one leaderboard would make the result look more precise than the evidence allows. This page therefore uses an evidence ledger: the source URL and date for a vendor statement, or the complete run fields for a local measurement. A missing field stays unknown rather than being filled from a review, a screenshot or a guessed conversion.

The measured local snapshot

Our published local observation is deliberately narrow: a three-second, 720p public-domain clip was processed as 36 frames in 87.4 seconds on an RTX 4090 reference machine, or 2.43 seconds per frame. It describes one batch run through the local Studio workflow at the recorded time. It does not say the pipeline is real-time, does not compare another GPU, and does not establish an in-game DLSS 5 frame rate. Repeating it requires the same source clip, output target, software version and hardware record.

What a future comparison must include

A credible run should preserve the original input and output, state the requested dimensions, name the model or preset, record the GPU and driver, include queue and retry time, and identify whether the result came from a game frame, a browser image workflow or local Studio. Review quality and speed separately. If there is no direct measurement, link the published source and mark the field unavailable. This keeps the center useful for AI readers without pretending that an illustrative image proves a performance claim.

Why there are no in-game frame rates here

We do not have the game runtime and controlled comparison scenes, so we do not publish unmeasured frame rates. Browser image results, the local Studio batch snapshot and in-game DLSS 5 are separate evidence tracks; none validates the others. Every number must be labelled as NVIDIA-published or measured by our own pipeline. For comparison, preserve source media, dimensions, model/preset, hardware, driver, software version, date, queue/retry time and output; keep unmeasured FPS and multipliers blank. The four quotations in the following table come from NVIDIA’s October update article: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/dlss-5-faster-ai-model-hogwarts-legacy-rtx-spark-laptops/ Checked 2026-10-26. These are NVIDIA’s statements, not observations made by this site.

At-a-glance comparison

Official wording (verbatim)What it saysSource and check date
DLSS 5’s 3D-Guided Neural Rendering model is now 10X faster overall compared to when it was announced in MarchNVIDIA says the model overall is faster than its March version; this does not mean games run ten times faster.NVIDIA · 2026-10-13 · checked 2026-10-26
The DLSS 5 October update shrinks the footprint by 24% to roughly 118 million parameters while reducing 4K VRAM usage by 20%NVIDIA reports a 24% smaller footprint, roughly 118 million parameters and 20% lower 4K VRAM usage.NVIDIA · 2026-10-13 · checked 2026-10-26
The result is half the GPU overhead of the September version while maintaining comparable visual fidelityNVIDIA reports half the GPU overhead relative to September, with comparable visual fidelity.NVIDIA · 2026-10-13 · checked 2026-10-26
boosting frame rates by up to 1.4XNVIDIA’s up to 1.4X frame-rate statement applies to NBA 2K27 + RTX 50 Series + RTX Spark laptops + GeForce NOW, not other games or GPUs.NVIDIA · 2026-10-13 · checked 2026-10-26

Turn the guide into a reviewable test

Inspect a cached example before uploading your own image; official technology claims and this site’s independent conversion results stay clearly separated.

Free visual enhancer → Game character style conversion → Source-linked GPU evidence checker → Download and local Studio guide → DLSS 5 APK and Android facts → DLSS 5 game support tracker → Game support tracker →

Sources and boundaries

  • NVIDIA DLSS 5 launch article ↗
  • NVIDIA DLSS 5 FAQ (September 2026; checked 2026-10-11) ↗

This is an independent reference. It is not an NVIDIA official page or partnership.

Frequently asked questions

Is this an FPS leaderboard?

No. The page does not publish unmeasured game FPS, multipliers or cross-GPU rankings.

What local measurement is available?

One RTX 4090 reference run processed 36 frames from a 3-second 720p clip in 87.4 seconds; it is batch context.

Can I compare a browser image result with DLSS 5 in a game?

No. They have different inputs and runtime contracts, so the page keeps them as separate evidence tracks.

What should I record for a new run?

Record input, output dimensions, model or preset, GPU, driver, software version, queue/retry time and date.

Why are some fields blank?

A blank or unknown field means no source or run record was available; it is not an invitation to infer a value.

Where are the source links?

Vendor references and the local workflow boundary are linked below; each future result should add its own evidence record.

DLSS5NVIDIA / AI Headshot Enhancer

Professional portrait workflow

AI Headshot Enhancer

Preview a free headshot example, then turn a soft selfie or compressed portrait into a cleaner profile image for a résumé, team page or professional profile. The workflow improves the source portrait instead of replacing your face with a new identity.

DLSS5NVIDIA is an independent browser-based DLSS 5-style effect converter, online visual enhancer and AI image generator for creating visual references from uploaded game frames and character images. It keeps structure, pose and identity as reviewable constraints while changing style, lighting and materials, and also offers separate upscale and restoration workflows. It is not an official NVIDIA DLSS runtime.

Enhance a headshot →

JPG, PNG and WebP · up to 10 MiB · review identity and skin texture before publishing

What is AI Headshot Enhancer?

AI Headshot Enhancer is a browser-based image quality enhancement workflow for people who already have a source image and need a controlled visual change. It uses a task-specific instruction rather than a blank prompt, so the requested output starts from the existing composition, subject or material. The page's before-and-after example is an illustrative reference; the result from your own file depends on its resolution, lighting, crop and visible detail.

How the workflow works

The workflow has three decisions. First, choose the largest original file instead of a screenshot or a second-generation social download. Next, confirm what is allowed to change and what must remain anchored: the task prompt is written for image quality enhancement, while the page shows the applicable input and output limits before submission. Finally, compare the source and result at 100 percent and download only after the information-sensitive areas pass your review. This order matters because a plausible AI result can look polished while still changing a face, label, edge or background.

Input, output and source quality

Use a clear JPG, PNG or WebP with enough pixels for the details you care about. For this page, the published intake note is: JPG, PNG and WebP · up to 10 MiB · review identity and skin texture before publishing. A clean input gives the model stronger evidence about edges, colour and texture. If the source is already heavily compressed, crop it tightly or find the original before spending a credit. Keep the source file beside the output; the service is an enhancement estimate, not a reversible edit history.

When to use this tool

  • Résumé and CV portraits
  • Team and company profile photos
  • LinkedIn profile images
  • Speaker and author bios

How it works

  1. Choose a recognizable portrait — Use a front-facing JPG, PNG or WebP with even light and enough resolution to see the face.
  2. Run the enhancement — Submit the portrait with the identity-preserving enhancement workflow. It uses 1 credit per task.
  3. Review before publishing — Compare eyes, jawline, hairline, skin texture, clothing and background before using the image professionally.

When this workflow fits

This workflow is a good fit for Résumé and CV portraits, Team and company profile photos, LinkedIn profile images, Speaker and author bios. It is especially useful when the subject is already recognizable and the job is to improve it while preserving the scene's main structure. It is less useful when the source has no recoverable detail, when the requested change is an exact measurement, or when the output will be used as an official record. In those cases, use the original capture, a design or editing application, or the receiving authority's own specification.

Limits and responsible use

Best when you already have a recognizable portrait and need a cleaner, more consistent profile image. It is an enhancement workflow, not a studio replacement or a guarantee of identity preservation. AI can alter faces and skin texture. Compare the output with the original and do not use it for identity verification or official documents. The service cannot guarantee that a small character, logo, number, face or repeated pattern will remain unchanged. A larger output also does not create new factual evidence; it creates a more usable visual estimate.

Credits and delivery

Your allowance and the task cost are shown before a signed-in job starts. The public example is available for comparison, while processing a personal file uses the displayed credit amount. A failed generation on our side is handled by the account workflow according to the billing policy. Check the output target and the source dimensions first so a task is not spent on a size you cannot use. For batch or API work, compare the per-image cost with storage, retries and your own review time.

A practical quality review

Before publishing, compare the result with the original in a fixed order: overall composition, subject identity, long straight edges, small text or labels, repeated texture, colour and shadows. Zooming to 100 percent exposes halos and invented marks that a thumbnail hides. For portraits, check eyes, teeth, hairline and skin texture. For products or architecture, check logos, windows, perspective and material boundaries. For generated edits, check that the requested change is present without unrelated objects or background drift.

Frequently asked questions

Is this an AI headshot generator?

Read the answer

It enhances an existing portrait. It does not promise a new set of poses, outfits or backgrounds, which makes the source identity easier to compare.

Can I use the result for a passport or ID?

Read the answer

No. Official documents have their own strict requirements. Use the dedicated passport photo tool and the receiving authority’s current rules instead.

How do I avoid an over-smoothed face?

Read the answer

Start with a sharp, evenly lit source and inspect the output at 100%. If skin texture looks plastic or the face shape moves, keep the original or try another source.

DLSS runtime DLL files: facts and email requests

These files are not a DLSS 5 unlocker or a crack; copying them into a game directory will not enable DLSS 5 in a game that does not support it.

They are NVIDIA’s original DLSS runtime libraries for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction and Frame Generation, forwarded unchanged.

Replacing DLLs may be blocked by anti-cheat, may cause crashes, and game updates may overwrite them; we provide no injectors, patches or bypass methods and promise no outcome.

Original-file inventory

Source: NVIDIA’s official SDK repository, lib/Windows_x86_64/rel/. Retrieved and checked on 2026-10-26. The files were not modified, renamed, patched or repackaged. DLSS5NVIDIA / AI Video Upscaler and Super-Resolution Workflow

Video super-resolution workflow

AI Video Upscaler and Super-Resolution Workflow

Generate or edit a short clip at a practical preview resolution, inspect the frames that matter, then finish the approved shot for delivery. This page shows the workflow and original reference demos while the live workspace currently processes still image frames.

Try a representative frame → Read the Seedance 2.5 cost guide →

The current public workspace processes still image frames. These clips are original silent reference demos for the planned video provider workflow.

What AI video upscaling changes

AI video upscaling is a frame-by-frame reconstruction workflow that enlarges a finished clip and estimates cleaner edges, texture and motion detail. It is different from native 4K rendering: the model can make a shot more usable, but it cannot prove detail that was absent from the source. The safest workflow keeps the original clip beside every enhanced export.

Why preview resolution comes first

A low-cost preview is useful when the creative decision is still changing. Generate at 480p or 720p, settle the prompt, camera move, reference images and timing, then choose the few frames that represent the shot. This avoids spending final-resolution credits on an idea that will be discarded.

Review time, not only one frame

Video quality is judged across time as well as in a single frame. Inspect faces, hands, typography, UI, hair, thin geometry and high-contrast edges at 100 percent. Scrub forward and backward around cuts and fast motion to catch flicker, warping, duplicate limbs or a subject whose identity drifts.

Document the final delivery

For a finished export, record the source resolution, target resolution, provider or model, frame rate and any crop. Keep an untouched master and label the result as AI-enhanced when the reconstruction changes uncertain detail. A 4K file is a delivery size, not a guarantee that every pixel is factual.

Test the hardest scene

Different scenes fail in different ways. Faces and hands expose identity errors; subtitles and game HUDs expose invented characters; foliage, hair and rain expose temporal shimmer; buildings and product edges expose ringing or oversharpening. Use a short representative clip from the hardest scene, rather than judging a clean establishing shot only.

Compare the whole cost

A cost comparison should include generation, retries, storage and the time spent checking bad frames. The preview-plus-finish route is useful when most ideas are rejected early, while native high-resolution generation may be simpler for a single approved shot. Keep the same prompt and frame-rate assumptions when comparing providers.

Keep the handoff reproducible

When a clip moves from generation to enhancement, pass along the original frame rate, aspect ratio, intended crop and any text-safe area. Do not silently change these between stages: a resize can make a timing problem look like a sharpness problem, and a crop can make a stable character appear to drift. Save a small contact sheet of approved key frames with the export so another editor can audit the result.

Use a final review checklist

Before publishing, write down the source and target dimensions, the frame rate, the number of frames processed and the review result for the hardest shot. Watch once with sound muted to focus on temporal structure, once at normal speed for motion, and once frame by frame around faces, text and fast cuts. This small record makes a later revision easier and keeps a cost comparison honest. It also gives a teammate enough context to reproduce the decision without guessing which version was approved.

Original reference demos

See the transition before you commit to a workflow

A practical 3-step video enhancement workflow

  1. 01

    Generate a preview

    Use 480p or 720p to iterate on prompt, camera movement, references and timing before paying for a final finish.

  2. 02

    Inspect key frames

    Check faces, hands, typography, thin geometry, fast motion and temporal consistency at 100%.

  3. 03

    Finish the approved shot

    Run the selected video super-resolution pass for 1080p or 4K delivery, then keep the original beside the AI-enhanced result.

Frequently asked questions

Can I upload a video and receive a finished 4K file now?

Read the answer

The public workspace currently supports still-image enhancement. This page documents the video workflow and shows original reference demos; use the frame workflow to test a representative shot while the video provider adapter is being connected.

Why generate at 480p or 720p before video super-resolution?

Read the answer

Lower-resolution previews make prompt, camera and timing iterations cheaper. Once a shot is approved, a separate super-resolution pass can finish the frames for 1080p or 4K delivery, with flicker and invented-detail checks before publishing.

Does video super-resolution equal native 4K generation?

Read the answer

No. It can recover and reconstruct useful detail, but small text, hair, thin lines and fast motion can change between frames. Keep the source clip, compare key frames at 100% and label the result as AI-enhanced.

DLSS5NVIDIA / Video Downloader

Media tool

Video Downloader

Paste the link to a video and get the file itself back — the rendition that site serves, at the quality you choose, with nothing re-encoded in between. One task takes up to three links, and nothing is uploaded: the link is the whole input.

DLSS5NVIDIA is an independent browser-based DLSS 5-style effect converter, online visual enhancer and AI image generator for creating visual references from uploaded game frames and character images. It keeps structure, pose and identity as reviewable constraints while changing style, lighting and materials, and also offers separate upscale and restoration workflows. It is not an official NVIDIA DLSS runtime.

Paste a video link →

YouTube, Bilibili, Douyin and TikTok · up to 3 links per task · 1 credit · the download link lasts about an hour

What is Video Downloader?

Video Downloader takes a video’s address and hands back the file that is being served there: the rendition the site holds, at the quality you choose, or the sound track on its own. It is not a player and not a converter — nothing is re-encoded, no frame is regenerated, and no image is uploaded, because the link is the entire input. What comes back is therefore decided by the source: it is the resolution, the frame rate and the container the platform itself publishes at that address.

How the workflow works

Copy the link from the browser, or from the app’s share menu. Paste up to three links in the studio, one per line, and choose a quality: best available, 1080p, 720p, 480p, 360p, or audio only. The task costs one credit, runs on a downloader outside this site’s own servers, and finishes in anything from fifteen seconds to a minute — the file has to be transferred, so the wait follows its size. What returns is a signed link, which the page plays back so you can check the picture and the sound before you save it.

Input, output and source quality

The input is a link, not a file: nothing from your device is uploaded, and no image is measured against a size limit. Accepted addresses are YouTube, Bilibili, Douyin and TikTok, including their short-link and mobile forms (youtu.be, b23.tv, v.douyin.com). A link from anywhere else is refused with a message naming those four rather than attempted, which is a deliberate choice about the sites we serve — the downloader behind the tool knows more places than we are willing to fetch from.

When to use this tool

  • Your own upload, kept as a file
  • A clip you have permission to reuse
  • Audio for transcribing or subtitling your own video
  • Offline copies where the platform and the licence allow it

How it works

  1. Copy the link — Open the video and copy the address from the browser, or use the app’s share menu. A short link such as youtu.be, b23.tv or v.douyin.com works as well.
  2. Paste it and pick a quality — Paste up to three links, one per line, then choose 1080p, 720p, 480p, 360p, the best available or audio only. The task costs 1 credit.
  3. Check the file and save it — The studio plays what came back so you can check picture and sound, then download it. The signed link expires after about an hour, and a later run fetches the file again.

When this workflow fits

This is a good fit for your own uploads, for a clip you have permission to reuse, for audio you need as a file in order to transcribe or subtitle your own video, and for an offline copy where the platform and the licence allow one. It is the wrong tool for a private, paid or member-only video, for a live stream, for anything you would have to redistribute to make useful, and for the case where you need one particular container or codec — the source site decides the format, not this page.

Limits and responsible use

The machine that performs the download is not ours and is not always reachable, so a task can fail quickly with a plain reason where another tool might hang; a confirmed failure refunds the credit. The finished file is delivered as a signed link that lasts about an hour, and we keep no copy of it afterwards — if you miss the window, run the link again and save the fresh copy. Sizes are real: a ten-minute clip measured 134 MiB at 1080p, 81 MiB at 720p, 25 MiB at 360p and 10 MiB as audio only. And the rights in the video never move: what you may do with the file afterwards is between you, the platform and the person who made it.

Credits and delivery

Every task costs 1 credit and accepts up to three links, so a batch of three is no dearer than one. A confirmed failure is refunded automatically under the account workflow, and the size of the video does not change the price — a ten-minute 1080p file and an audio-only track cost the same. Your allowance is shown before a signed-in task starts.

A practical quality review

Play what came back before you rely on it: check that the picture and the sound run to the end, that the resolution matches the quality you asked for, and that the frame rate and the audio are the ones you need. Check the container as well — a YouTube 1080p file arrives as WebM with AV1 video and Opus audio — and convert it yourself if your editor wants something else. Then save the file, because the signed link expires about an hour after the task finished.

Frequently asked questions

Which sites can I paste a link from?

Read the answer

YouTube, Bilibili, Douyin and TikTok, including their short-link and mobile addresses. Other sites are refused with a message that names the four rather than attempted: the downloader behind this tool could handle more, but we choose which sites we fetch from.

Is downloading a video legal?

Read the answer

It depends on the video and on where you are. Download only material you have the right to download — your own uploads, clips you have permission to reuse, or work offered under a licence that allows it. We do not host the file and we cannot give you rights in someone else’s work.

Why does the download link expire?

Read the answer

The finished file is handed to your browser as a signed link to our storage, valid for about an hour. That is deliberate: it is a delivery channel rather than a library. If it expires before you save the file, run the link again and download the fresh copy.

What format and resolution do I get?

Read the answer

Whatever the site serves for the quality you chose, with nothing re-encoded. A YouTube 1080p video arrives as WebM with AV1 video and Opus audio, 360p as the smaller rendition of the same clip, and audio-only as the sound track on its own. Your own container choice is therefore not on offer — the source decides it.

What happens if the download fails?

Read the answer

A confirmed failure refunds the credit automatically and shows the reason. The worker that fetches the file is a machine that is not always reachable, so a task can fail quickly with a plain reason instead of hanging; running the same link again is the fix.

DLSS5NVIDIA / AI Image Tools Compared
Independent guide · updated October 2026

AI image tools compared

DLSS 5 is an in-game neural rendering technology. GPT Image, ChatGPT Images, Midjourney and FLUX create or edit images. This guide compares their jobs instead of treating them as interchangeable products, then gives you a real sample and a checklist to run yourself.

Try before you choose

Run a conversion, inspect the pixels, then read the table

The examples are cached so you can see the workflow before signing in. Use the character sample for style conversion, the enhancer sample for existing images, or open the source-led gallery when you want to audit published references.

Try character conversion → Try visual enhancer → Open 20-pair gallery →

Choose by task

What each workflow is actually for

ToolPrimary roleBest forTypical workflow
DLSS 5 (official technology)Game neural renderingRTX 50 series gamesGame frames, lighting and materials
GPT Image 2Image generation and editingComplex prompts and editsAPI and ChatGPT workflows
ChatGPT Images 2.5Conversational image creationIterative revisionsNatural-language editing
MidjourneyCreative image generationConcept art and styleVisual exploration
FLUXHosted image generationDeveloper pipelinesCustom workflows
Browser AI upscalerImage enhancementExisting photos and rendersFast enlargement without a GPU

Hardware context

Ground the comparison in GPU evidence

The table explains each workflow. For model-level DLSS 5 status, VRAM and source links, continue to the independent GPU evidence checker.

Check GPU evidence by model →

Evidence, not a leaderboard

Three ways to inspect the claim

A useful comparison lets a reader see the source, run a related task and understand the boundary of the result. These are independent references, not a claim that one model wins every prompt.

20 source-linked reference pairs

Keep the NVIDIA source link beside every pair and inspect faces, hair, thin geometry, materials and shadows at 100%.

Open the source-led gallery →

A browser result you can inspect

Use the same before-and-after checks for product labels, faces and straight edges before deciding whether an enhancement is useful.

Open the free enhancer →

Style conversion keeps the source visible

The independent workflow changes style, lighting and material direction while keeping the original frame available for review.

See the character cases →

Repeatable review

Use the same four checks every time

01

Structure

Does the output keep the pose, silhouette, perspective and repeated geometry?

02

Identity

Do faces, hands, logos and product labels stay recognisable against the source?

03

Texture

Are edges and materials clearer, or has the model invented plausible detail?

04

Workflow

Can a visitor run a comparable input, inspect the result and keep the original?

One measured snapshot

The local DLSS5 Studio workflow processed one 3-second, 720p public-domain clip as 36 frames in 87.4 seconds on an RTX 4090 reference machine — about 2.43 seconds per frame. That is a batch-workflow observation, not a real-time promise or a cross-provider benchmark.

Read the full Studio evidence →

Comparison questions

Is DLSS 5 the same thing as an AI image generator?

No. Official DLSS is an in-game neural-rendering technology. Image generators create or edit images from prompts, while the independent browser workflow on this site converts a supplied frame or reference into a reviewable visual direction.

How can I compare tools fairly?

Keep the source image, aspect ratio, target direction and review checks fixed. Compare structure, identity, texture and workflow separately instead of judging two unrelated prompts from different models.

Are the examples on this page a benchmark?

No. The gallery combines publicly published NVIDIA reference pairs with independent browser examples. A local Studio run is reported as one measured snapshot, not a universal speed or quality claim.

Can I try a result before creating an account?

Yes. The character conversion and visual-enhancer examples use cached sample runs. You can inspect the before-and-after result first, then sign in when you want to upload your own image.

DLSS and NVIDIA are trademarks of NVIDIA Corporation. This site is independent and non-official. Public NVIDIA reference images remain the property of their respective owners; the browser examples are independent references.

Legal

Privacy Policy

This policy explains what ColorReco Tech collects when you use www.dlss5nvidia.com, why, and what you can ask us to do about it.

1. What we collect

  • Account data: email, display name, sign-in provider and internal account identifier.
  • Billing data: plan, credit balance, subscription identifiers and processor status. Card numbers stay on the processor page.
  • Content you submit: uploaded images, prompts, generation settings and results.
  • Technical data: IP address, browser and language, pages opened and limited usage events.
  • Support messages sent to support@dlss5nvidia.com.

2. Why we use it

We do not sell personal data or use images and prompts to train models.

  • To authenticate you, process images, keep history and balances correct.
  • To bill, grant and deduct credits, and prevent fraud.
  • To keep the service stable and secure through rate limiting, abuse detection and error diagnosis.
  • To improve features with aggregated analytics and send necessary service notices.

3. Who processes it for us

These providers may process data outside your country under their own policies and our instructions.

  • Google Firebase for authentication and the account database.
  • PayPal, Stripe and Dodo Payments for payments and subscriptions.
  • Vercel for hosting and content delivery.
  • Model and storage providers for image jobs and temporary files.
  • Google Analytics for aggregated visitor statistics.

4. Cookies and local storage

Necessary storage keeps you signed in and remembers your language. Analytics storage counts visits and feature use. You can block or clear storage in your browser.

5. How long we keep it

  • Account and billing records while the account exists and as long as tax, accounting or fraud rules require.
  • Uploaded files and results until deletion or account closure.
  • Server and error logs for a short operational window, then rolling deletion.
  • Analytics data according to the analytics tool retention setting.

6. Your rights

Write to support@dlss5nvidia.com from your account address to access, correct, export or delete data, or object to a use. We answer within 30 days. EU and UK residents can also complain to their data protection authority.

7. Security

Traffic is encrypted in transit, provider API keys stay on the server, and production access is restricted. If a breach affects your data, we will notify you and the competent authority without undue delay.

8. Children

The service is not intended for anyone under 18 or the local age of majority. We do not knowingly collect children’s data; tell us if you believe a child has an account.

9. Changes and contact

We update this policy when processing changes. Controller and contact: ColorReco Tech, support@dlss5nvidia.com.

Last updated September 20, 2026. Questions about this document: support@dlss5nvidia.com.

Method and reproduction

Inputs come from uploads to our own image pipeline. For a reproduction, record the original input, output size, model or preset, hardware, driver, date and elapsed time; these are not NVIDIA runtime screenshots, game frames or cross-GPU comparisons.

Open the benchmark evidence center → · See 20 character-style cases →

Six-second video references

The clips loop and carry a text conclusion so the page remains understandable without playback.

Our only published video-pipeline measurement: a three-second 720p clip (36 frames) took 87.4 seconds of batch time on an RTX 4090 reference machine with driver 591.86 — 2.43 seconds per frame. That is local batch time, not real-time performance, and not the render time of the two clips above, which are transition references only.

Measurement method and limits: open the benchmark evidence center →

Honest limits

Very small sources, heavy compression, tiny text, multiple faces and motion blur can make results unreliable. Enlargement is an estimate, not factual recovery; inspect at 100% and keep the original before publishing.

Frequently asked questions

Are these NVIDIA DLSS 5 runtime screenshots?

No. These are independent before-and-after references from the DLSS5NVIDIA image pipeline. They are not NVIDIA captures and do not prove an in-game DLSS runtime result.

What does “before and after” mean here?

Each card keeps the input beside one output from the named workflow. The three low/high pairs show verified file dimensions; the retouch, cutout, erase and try-on cards show measured workflow runs with their controls and date.

Does upscaling recover factual detail?

No. It estimates a more usable visual result from the input. Faces, labels, numbers, thin geometry and repeated patterns can change, so compare them at 100% and keep the original.

Can I try the converter without an RTX GPU?

Yes. The browser workflow runs on the site service, so a modern browser is enough for a cached example or an account workflow. The separate DLSS5 Studio request page is a Windows RTX product and is still being developed.

Why is the retouch card not labelled as an upscale?

Its input and output are both 600 × 900. It is a same-size portrait retouch case, included to show the difference between restoring an existing image and enlarging it.

What inputs usually fail?

Extremely small or heavily compressed images, tiny text, multiple faces and scenes with motion blur are hard cases. Start with the largest original file, then inspect the result before sharing or publishing it.

How is this page different from the benchmark center?

This page is a visual gallery: it pairs existing inputs and outputs so you can inspect edges, faces and composition. The benchmark center defines measurement fields and separates recorded runs from visual references.

Can I reproduce one of these cases?

Yes. Open the linked tool on a comparable input, use the control shown on the card, and record the original file, output size, model or preset, hardware, driver, date and elapsed time. Results may vary between runs.

Why does this page not use NVIDIA screenshots?

The gallery documents our own image pipeline. Keeping independent assets separate from NVIDIA material makes the provenance clear and avoids presenting a visual reference as an official runtime capture.

DLSS5NVIDIA / AI Image Upscaler

AI image tool

AI Image Upscaler

Turn a small or compressed image into a larger, cleaner version while keeping the original framing, colors and composition.

DLSS5NVIDIA is an independent browser-based DLSS 5-style effect converter, online visual enhancer and AI image generator for creating visual references from uploaded game frames and character images. It keeps structure, pose and identity as reviewable constraints while changing style, lighting and materials, and also offers separate upscale and restoration workflows. It is not an official NVIDIA DLSS runtime.

Upload an image →Try free example →

JPG, PNG and WebP · up to 10 MiB · 1536 px maximum output edge

The reference example runs without an account; your own upload requires sign-in.

Where does this tool fit in the product?

This upscaler is a limited entry point for enlarging an existing image and reviewing the result against its source. The product’s main workflow is style conversion and neural-render redraw, with DLSS5 Studio as the desktop handover. Generated detail is an estimate, not pixel-exact recovery or the NVIDIA DLSS game runtime.

Explore style conversion and neural-render redraw · See the DLSS5 Studio desktop workflow

Last checked: 2026-10-23

What is AI Image Upscaler?

AI Image Upscaler is a browser-based image upscaling workflow for people who already have a source image and need a controlled visual change. It uses a task-specific instruction rather than a blank prompt, so the requested output starts from the existing composition, subject or material. The page's before-and-after example is an illustrative reference; the result from your own file depends on its resolution, lighting, crop and visible detail.

How the workflow works

The workflow has three decisions. First, choose the largest original file instead of a screenshot or a second-generation social download. Next, confirm what is allowed to change and what must remain anchored: the task prompt is written for image upscaling, while the page shows the applicable input and output limits before submission. Finally, compare the source and result at 100 percent and download only after the information-sensitive areas pass your review. This order matters because a plausible AI result can look polished while still changing a face, label, edge or background.

Input, output and source quality

Use a clear JPG, PNG or WebP with enough pixels for the details you care about. For this page, the published intake note is: JPG, PNG and WebP · up to 10 MiB · 1536 px maximum output edge. A clean input gives the model stronger evidence about edges, colour and texture. If the source is already heavily compressed, crop it tightly or find the original before spending a credit. Keep the source file beside the output; the service is an enhancement estimate, not a reversible edit history.

When to use this tool

  • Small photos
  • Product listings
  • Real estate images
  • Screenshots and scans

How it works

  1. Choose your image — Select a JPG, PNG or WebP and check its dimensions. The preview stays in your browser.
  2. Confirm the output size — Choose a 2× or 4× target, capped at 1536 px per edge. Sign in and confirm the 1-credit task.
  3. Compare and download — Review the result at 100%, especially faces and text, then download your image.

When this workflow fits

This workflow is a good fit for Small photos, Product listings, Real estate images, Screenshots and scans. It is especially useful when the subject is already recognizable and the job is to enlarge it while preserving the scene's main structure. It is less useful when the source has no recoverable detail, when the requested change is an exact measurement, or when the output will be used as an official record. In those cases, use the original capture, a design or editing application, or the receiving authority's own specification.

Limits and responsible use

AI can change uncertain details, so large edges, repeated geometry and output dimensions need a deliberate check. Do not treat a generated result as pixel-exact recovery. If a detail cannot be verified against the original, keep the original or run another source through the workflow. The service cannot guarantee that a small character, logo, number, face or repeated pattern will remain unchanged. A larger output also does not create new factual evidence; it creates a more usable visual estimate.

Credits and delivery

Your allowance and the task cost are shown before a signed-in job starts. The public example is available for comparison, while processing a personal file uses the displayed credit amount. A failed generation on our side is handled by the account workflow according to the billing policy. Check the output target and the source dimensions first so a task is not spent on a size you cannot use. For batch or API work, compare the per-image cost with storage, retries and your own review time.

A practical quality review

Before publishing, compare the result with the original in a fixed order: overall composition, subject identity, long straight edges, small text or labels, repeated texture, colour and shadows. Zooming to 100 percent exposes halos and invented marks that a thumbnail hides. For portraits, check eyes, teeth, hairline and skin texture. For products or architecture, check logos, windows, perspective and material boundaries. For generated edits, check that the requested change is present without unrelated objects or background drift.

Frequently asked questions

What does an AI image upscaler do?

Read the answer

It generates a larger version of an image while reconstructing plausible edges and texture. It is useful for low-resolution photos, screenshots and product images, but it cannot recover detail that was never captured with certainty.

Can I upscale an image for free?

Read the answer

You can compare the illustrative example without an account. Processing your own image requires sign-in and uses 1 credit per task. Your allowance is shown before you submit.

Does upscaling change the composition?

Read the answer

The enhancement preset asks the model to keep the composition, framing, colors and subject identity unchanged. Always review faces, text and fine product details before publishing.

DLSS5NVIDIA is an independent browser-based DLSS 5-style effect converter, online visual enhancer and AI image generator for creating visual references from uploaded game frames and character images. What is DLSS 5 Visual Enhancer Online?

DLSS 5 Visual Enhancer Online is a browser-based image quality enhancement workflow for people who already have a source image and need a controlled visual change. It uses a task-specific instruction rather than a blank prompt, so the requested output starts from the existing composition, subject or material. Finally, compare the source and result at 100 percent and download only after the information-sensitive areas pass your review. This order matters because a plausible AI result can look polished while still changing a face, label, edge or background.

Input, output and source quality

Use a clear JPG, PNG or WebP with enough pixels for the details you care about. For this page, the published intake note is: JPG, PNG and WebP · 1536 px maximum output edge · 1 credit per task. A clean input gives the model stronger evidence about edges, colour and texture. If the source is already heavily compressed, crop it tightly or find the original before spending a credit. Keep the source file beside the output; the service is an enhancement estimate, not a reversible edit history.

When to use this tool

  • Compressed social photos
  • Marketplace product images
  • Old family photos
  • Slides and screenshots

How it works

  1. Choose your image — Select a JPG, PNG or WebP and check its dimensions. The preview stays in your browser.
  2. Confirm the output size — Choose a 2× or 4× target, capped at 1536 px per edge. Sign in and confirm the 1-credit task.
  3. Compare and download — Review the result at 100%, especially faces and text, then download your image.

When this workflow fits

This workflow is a good fit for Compressed social photos, Marketplace product images, Old family photos, Slides and screenshots. It is especially useful when the subject is already recognizable and the job is to improve it while preserving the scene's main structure. It is less useful when the source has no recoverable detail, when the requested change is an exact measurement, or when the output will be used as an official record. In those cases, use the original capture, a design or editing application, or the receiving authority's own specification.

Limits and responsible use

AI can change uncertain details, so faces, labels, text and uncertain texture need a deliberate check. Do not treat a generated result as pixel-exact recovery. If a detail cannot be verified against the original, keep the original or run another source through the workflow. The service cannot guarantee that a small character, logo, number, face or repeated pattern will remain unchanged. A larger output also does not create new factual evidence; it creates a more usable visual estimate.

Your allowance and the task cost are shown before a signed-in job starts. The public example is available for comparison, while processing a personal file uses the displayed credit amount. A practical quality review

Before publishing, compare the result with the original in a fixed order: overall composition, subject identity, long straight edges, small text or labels, repeated texture, colour and shadows. Zooming to 100 percent exposes halos and invented marks that a thumbnail hides. For portraits, check eyes, teeth, hairline and skin texture. For products or architecture, check logos, windows, perspective and material boundaries. For generated edits, check that the requested change is present without unrelated objects or background drift.

The enhancement instruction asks to preserve the scene, but AI enhancement can make uncertain detail look plausible. Check logos, faces, numbers and other information-sensitive areas at 100%.

DLSS5NVIDIA / 20 Game Character Style Conversion Cases

Game character style conversion

20 Game Character Style Conversion Cases

Use these original before-and-after pairs to evaluate character style conversion: keep the pose, costume and identity anchored while changing lighting, materials, palette and world direction.

Asset note: These 20 pairs are original visual references for evaluating a conversion brief. They are not NVIDIA DLSS 5 captures and do not claim a DLSS 5 runtime integration.

Try your own character frame → See the video enhancement workflow →

One cyberpunk direction runs as a free cached example — no account needed.

What game character style conversion means

Game character style conversion changes the visual language of an existing character while preserving the parts that make the character recognisable. A useful conversion keeps the silhouette, pose, costume construction, camera and identity stable, then changes lighting, materials, palette, environment and rendering direction. These examples are original visual references for planning and review; they are not official NVIDIA captures or a claim of DLSS runtime processing.

Lock the identity before changing the style

Start by writing an invariant brief. Name the character, camera angle, pose, major costume pieces, face shape, hair outline and equipment that must survive the conversion. Separating these constraints from style variables prevents a prompt from accidentally redesigning the character while it is trying to change the world around them.

Change visual variables deliberately

Treat style as a controlled set of variables: cinematic rim light, cel-shaded edges, worn metal, translucent fabric, neon bounce, painterly texture or realistic skin response. Change one or two variables at a time, compare against the base frame, and keep a version that proves the prompt still respects the original composition.

How to review a conversion

Review a result at thumbnail size and at 100 percent. At a glance, the pose and visual hierarchy should read immediately. At full size, inspect eyes, fingers, facial proportions, weapon silhouettes, armour seams and cloth folds. If the image will become a video, review several frames for flicker and identity drift before calling the conversion usable.

DLSS5NVIDIA / DLSS 5 support status: what is confirmed?

Source-led independent guide

DLSS 5 support status: what is confirmed?

This tracker records what an official source actually says, when we checked it and where the wording remains provisional. Unknown is a valid result.

A dated DLSS 5 status tracker that separates NVIDIA’s confirmed statements, planned expansion and unknown model-level details.

DLSS 5 release date timeline: dated status changes

Last checked: 2026-10-26. Status follows the official article body. A news excerpt, preview demonstration or elapsed planned date does not establish a release.

DateEvent that happenedSourceChecked
2026-03-16NVIDIA published the DLSS 5 announcement and its planned game list. This records an announcement, not those games becoming available.NVIDIA source (march)2026-10-26
2026-10-13NVIDIA published an update confirming NBA 2K27 had launched the feature in September and announcing subsequent model, Hogwarts Legacy, Where Winds Meet and RTX Remix updates. Those announcements are recorded here, not their later completion.NVIDIA source (october)2026-10-26

Official headline wording: 2X Faster Model. This is NVIDIA’s claim about its October neural-rendering model, involving pipeline/model changes and a planned NBA 2K27 rollout with named hardware. It is not a claim that every game doubles its frame rate, or a performance result from this site. The separate Frame Generation beta does not establish DLSS 5 neural-rendering support. NVIDIA source (october)

This tracks vendor game features. Our game-character style conversion is an independent image workflow, not an installation or emulation of NVIDIA’s game runtime.

Check the DLSS 5 supported games tracker

Confirmed debut

NBA 2K27 on September 3, 2026, with DLSS Neural Rendering and driver 616.64 WHQL.

Confirmed hardware scope

NVIDIA’s FAQ says all GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs and laptops, plus GeForce NOW Ultimate on RTX 5080 rigs.

Planned expansion (checked 2026-10-11)

The same FAQ says NVIDIA plans to work on expanding official support to RTX 40 Series after RTX 50 tuning. The timing is unspecified, so this remains a future plan rather than current support.

How to interpret the RTX 40 statement

The FAQ wording is an official future plan: NVIDIA says it will work on expanding official support to GeForce RTX 40 Series once RTX 50 Series performance is more fully tuned. It does not give a date, a driver version or a list of games. We therefore show the plan as useful context while keeping the current model-level result unconfirmed. That distinction is deliberate: a planned expansion should not be read as a present-tense compatibility guarantee.

At-a-glance comparison

ClaimStatusSource boundary
NBA 2K27 launchConfirmedNVIDIA launch article and September FAQ
RTX 50 Series / laptopsConfirmed for the documented launch scopeNVIDIA September FAQ
RTX 40 Series official supportPlanned, not current confirmedNVIDIA September FAQ
RTX 30 and older official DLSS 5 supportUnknown / not published here as supportedNo matching official model-level statement in our reviewed sources

Turn the guide into a reviewable test

Inspect a cached example before uploading your own image; official technology claims and this site’s independent conversion results stay clearly separated.

Free visual enhancer → Game character style conversion → Source-linked GPU evidence checker → Download and local Studio guide → DLSS 5 APK and Android facts → DLSS 5 game support tracker →

Sources and boundaries

  • NVIDIA DLSS 5 launch article ↗
  • NVIDIA DLSS 5 FAQ (September 2026; checked 2026-10-11) ↗

This is an independent reference. It is not an NVIDIA official page or partnership.

Frequently asked questions

Why does the tracker use unknown?

Because a plausible inference is not an official source. Unknown prevents an unsupported compatibility claim from becoming a search snippet.

How often is this page updated?

Only when a source is rechecked. The review date and source link stay with the claim.

Where can I inspect a GPU model?

Use the sister GPU evidence checker for model-level VRAM, architecture and source links.

DLSS5NVIDIA / Integration guide

Integration

The image API, on one page

Nine image models behind one asynchronous API: open an upload ticket, put the bytes, submit the task, poll it, fetch the signed result. This page is what an integrator reads; the gateway is what it calls. Both — and the JSON below — are rendered from one catalog file, so they cannot disagree. Every number here is a measurement with its date.

Two entry points

  • Read — this page, /api-catalog.json for every model, and /api-catalog/<model>.json for one. No key required.
  • Call — https://dashboard.alphanetplus.com: sign in, copy the project API key, then GET /v1/models with it to list the model ids that key may use.
FactValue
Calls go tohttps://dashboard.alphanetplus.com
AuthenticationAuthorization: Bearer <project API key>
Price$0.01 per call
Upload ceiling10 MiB per reference image
Result URLssigned, and they expire 900 s after the task finishes
Catalog version2026-09-26.1 (updated 2026-09-26)

The four steps

  1. 1. Open an upload ticket — POST /v1/flux/uploads
    One ticket per reference image. The response carries the URL to PUT the bytes to, the file id you submit, and the byte ceiling.
  2. 2. Upload the bytes — PUT {upload_url}
    Send the file itself to the signed URL, with the headers from the ticket. Nothing else goes through our API: the bytes go straight to storage.
  3. 3. Submit the task — POST /v1/tasks/alphanet-flux
    The model id and the file ids in order. Always send an Idempotency-Key: the same key and body return the same task, a different body under the same key is refused with 409.
  4. 4. Poll, then fetch the result — GET /v1/tasks/{task_id}
    Poll until the status is terminal, then read /v1/tasks/{task_id}/result for the signed URLs and the sha256 of each artifact.

The nine models

ModelWhat you getReferencesMeasured
flux-kleinGenerative edit, upscale and restore1–4~16 s end to end for a 1152 × 1536 render, 6.4 s of it inference (measured 2026-09-26); the rest is queueing and the result upload
pixrestore-sDetail restore1~3.5 s for a 3131 × 1549 frame (measured 2026-09-17, end to end)
cutout-fastBackground removal1~5 s end to end, 0.8 s of it inference (measured 2026-09-26)
erase-qualityGenerative erase1~54 s end to end, 50 s of it inference (measured 2026-09-22)
vectorize-fastImage to SVG1~7 s end to end, 0.4 s of it tracing (measured 2026-09-22)
tryon-qualityVirtual try-on2~69 s end to end, 59 s of it inference (measured 2026-09-26)
interior-qualityInterior render1–2~59 s of inference (measured 2026-09-25)
retouch-qualityPortrait retouch1~79 s end to end, 61 s of it inference (measured 2026-09-25)
makeup-qualityVirtual makeup1–2~62 s of inference (measured 2026-09-25)

Model by model

flux-klein — Generative edit, upscale and restore

The general-purpose editor: your prompt decides what happens, and the output is the size you ask for.

Capability generative_repaint · verified 2026-09-26 (public gateway) · JSON for this model

References

  1. image_ids[0] — the image to edit

Returns: PNG or WebP at the width and height you sent; 1–4 references may be combined.

Measured: ~16 s end to end for a 1152 × 1536 render, 6.4 s of it inference (measured 2026-09-26); the rest is queueing and the result upload

Parameters

FieldTypeValuesDefaultNotes
prompt (required)string——What should change. The only model here that reads your own words.
widthinteger—1024Output width: a multiple of 16, at most 1536 px.
heightinteger—1024Output height, under the same rules.
num_inference_stepsinteger—4Four steps unless you ask for more; more steps refine detail and take longer.
seedinteger——Same seed and body reproduces the same render.
max_sequence_lengthinteger——
output_formatstringpng | webp—
output_qualityinteger——

Where it stops

  • It is a generative re-render: faces and small text can shift. Review the result at 100% before publishing.
  • It cannot add detail that was never captured with certainty — an upscale reconstructs plausible texture, not the original pixels.

Open the enhancer in the studio

pixrestore-s — Detail restore

Renders a sharper, cleaner version of an image at its own size. No prompt, no knobs beyond steps.

Capability detail_restore · verified 2026-09-17 (public gateway, 8/8 with the idempotency pair) · JSON for this model

References

  1. image_ids[0] — the image

Returns: PNG at the input size.

Measured: ~3.5 s for a 3131 × 1549 frame (measured 2026-09-17, end to end)

Parameters

FieldTypeValuesDefaultNotes
num_inference_stepsinteger1–41One pass is the service default, and on this model one pass measured better than four on 2026-09-17 — more steps is not more detail here.
seedinteger——

Refused, not ignored: width, height, max_sequence_length, output_format, output_quality — sending one fails the call instead of being dropped.

Where it stops

  • The result is "clearer", not "faithful": detail is generated, so fine text and small patterns can change. It is not a lossless enlarger.
  • It does not resize: send the size you want to keep, or upscale separately.

cutout-fast — Background removal

Cuts the subject out and answers a PNG with an alpha channel at the input size.

Capability tool_cutout · verified 2026-09-26 (public gateway) · JSON for this model

References

  1. image_ids[0] — the photo

Returns: PNG with transparency, at the input size — 768 × 1024 in, 768 × 1024 out.

Measured: ~5 s end to end, 0.8 s of it inference (measured 2026-09-26)

Parameters

FieldTypeValuesDefaultNotes
bg_colorstring——Fill the removed background with a colour instead of leaving it transparent.
bg_modelstring——Which matting model the service picks (isnet, birefnet or u2net family).
alpha_mattingstring——Softer edges on hair and fur, at a little more time.

Refused, not ignored: width, height, max_sequence_length, output_format, output_quality — sending one fails the call instead of being dropped.

Where it stops

  • Fine hair, glass and motion blur keep some background; a see-through subject cannot be cut cleanly.
  • The cut is the whole frame. There is no per-object selection: one subject per call.

Remove a background in the studio

erase-quality — Generative erase

Names what should go; the model removes it and rebuilds the surface underneath.

Capability tool_erase · verified 2026-09-22 (public gateway, 8/8) · JSON for this model

References

  1. image_ids[0] — the photo

Returns: PNG at a fixed 1024 × 1024, whatever the input size was.

Measured: ~54 s end to end, 50 s of it inference (measured 2026-09-22)

Parameters

FieldTypeValuesDefaultNotes
prompt (required)string——The object or mark to remove.
num_inference_stepsinteger4–208
seedinteger——

Refused, not ignored: width, height, max_sequence_length, output_format, output_quality — sending one fails the call instead of being dropped.

Where it stops

  • The whole frame is re-rendered at 1024², so a larger original comes back at that size and fine text elsewhere can drift.
  • It removes what you name; it does not understand "remove the person but keep the shadow".

Erase an object in the studio

vectorize-fast — Image to SVG

Traces a bitmap into real vector paths and answers an SVG — so it scales to any size without blurring.

Capability tool_vectorize · verified 2026-09-22 (public gateway, 8/8) · JSON for this model

References

  1. image_ids[0] — the bitmap

Returns: image/svg+xml. The SVG declares its own width and height, so the JSON result reports width/height as null.

Measured: ~7 s end to end, 0.4 s of it tracing (measured 2026-09-22)

Parameters

FieldTypeValuesDefaultNotes
presetstringlogo | illustration | photologoA fixed parameter set on the service, not free text.
max_edgeinteger256–20481024Long edge the trace runs at; larger input is downscaled to it.
colorsinteger2–64—
filter_speckleinteger0–32—Drops specks smaller than this many pixels.

Refused, not ignored: width, height, max_sequence_length, output_format, output_quality — sending one fails the call instead of being dropped.

Where it stops

  • A photograph comes back posterised: the photo preset limits the palette to 16 colours before tracing.
  • The output is paths, not an embedded bitmap — expect a small file for a logo and a large one for a picture.

Convert an image in the studio

tryon-quality — Virtual try-on

Puts the garment from one photo onto the person in another. Two references, in order, and no prompt.

Capability tool_tryon · verified 2026-09-26 (public gateway, re-measured); the 10/10 pass including the idempotency pair was 2026-09-25 · JSON for this model

References

  1. image_ids[0] — person
  2. image_ids[1] — garment

Returns: PNG shaped like the person photo (3:4 → 768 × 1024). Face, hair, pose, other clothing and background are asked to stay identical.

Measured: ~69 s end to end, 59 s of it inference (measured 2026-09-26)

Parameters

FieldTypeValuesDefaultNotes
garment_typestringtop | bottom | dress | outfittopWhich part of the outfit the reference replaces. Omitted, the reference is read as a top.
aspectstring1:1 | 3:4 | 4:3 | 2:3 | 3:2 | 16:9 | 9:16—Optional. Omitted, the output follows the person photo’s shape — a 3:4 portrait comes back 768 × 1024.
seedinteger——

Refused, not ignored: prompt, width, height, num_inference_steps, max_sequence_length, output_format, output_quality — sending one fails the call instead of being dropped.

Where it stops

  • One garment per call: the reference is read as a single piece, so a top and a bottom need two calls.
  • The order of image_ids is the meaning — person first, garment second. Swapping them changes the result, not the error.
  • Layered outfits, heavy shadows across the garment and unusual poses are the hard cases.

Try it on in the studio

interior-quality — Interior render

Turns an empty or unfinished room into a furnished render in a named style, keeping the architecture where it is.

Capability tool_interior · verified 2026-09-25 (public gateway, 8/8) · JSON for this model

References

  1. image_ids[0] — room
  2. image_ids[1] — style reference (optional)

Returns: PNG shaped like the room photo (3:2 → 1152 × 768), with walls, windows, doors, ceiling line and camera angle held.

Measured: ~59 s of inference (measured 2026-09-25)

Parameters

FieldTypeValuesDefaultNotes
stylestringnordic | cream | japandi | chinese | industrial | frenchnordicEach style is a fixed recipe of materials, furniture and lighting.
room_typestringliving_room | bedroom | dining_room | study | kitchen | bathroom | kids_room | balconyliving_room
extrastring——Up to 120 characters of extra brief, folded into the fixed instruction. Longer is refused: it would start to override the parts that hold the room in place.
aspectstring1:1 | 3:4 | 4:3 | 2:3 | 3:2 | 16:9 | 9:16—Optional. Omitted, the output follows the room photo’s shape — 3:2 comes back 1152 × 768.
seedinteger——

Refused, not ignored: prompt, width, height, num_inference_steps, max_sequence_length, output_format, output_quality — sending one fails the call instead of being dropped.

Where it stops

  • Start from the emptiest frame you have: a room that is already furnished comes back redesigned rather than built on.
  • The second reference steers palette and materials only — it cannot add a wall or move a window.
  • It is a visualisation, not a measured plan: sockets, floor coverings and furniture proportions can differ from the building.

Render a room in the studio

retouch-quality — Portrait retouch

Cleans up a portrait — skin, under-eyes, eyes, stray hairs — without changing the face.

Capability tool_retouch · verified 2026-09-25 (public gateway, 8/8) · JSON for this model

References

  1. image_ids[0] — portrait

Returns: PNG shaped like the portrait, with skin grain kept.

Measured: ~79 s end to end, 61 s of it inference (measured 2026-09-25)

Parameters

FieldTypeValuesDefaultNotes
levelstringlight | natural | strongnatural
aspectstring1:1 | 3:4 | 4:3 | 2:3 | 3:2 | 16:9 | 9:16—Optional. Omitted, the output follows the portrait’s shape (fallback 1:1).
seedinteger——

Refused, not ignored: prompt, width, height, num_inference_steps, max_sequence_length, output_format, output_quality — sending one fails the call instead of being dropped.

Where it stops

  • It will not slim a face, widen the eyes or change a hairstyle: that is the instruction, not a setting.
  • It does not add makeup — that is the separate virtual-makeup model.
  • A heavy filter look is refused on purpose; the result keeps visible texture.

Retouch a portrait in the studio

makeup-quality — Virtual makeup

Applies a named makeup look to a face, optionally matched from a reference photo.

Capability tool_makeup · verified 2026-09-25 (public gateway, 8/8) · JSON for this model

References

  1. image_ids[0] — portrait
  2. image_ids[1] — makeup reference (optional)

Returns: PNG shaped like the portrait. Identity, expression, hair, clothing, framing and lighting are asked to stay as they are.

Measured: ~62 s of inference (measured 2026-09-25)

Parameters

FieldTypeValuesDefaultNotes
lookstringdaily | korean | glam | bridal | latte | retrodailyA fixed recipe of base, contour, brows, eyeshadow, liner, lashes and lip.
intensitystringlight | medium | strongmedium
aspectstring1:1 | 3:4 | 4:3 | 2:3 | 3:2 | 16:9 | 9:16—Optional. Omitted, the output follows the portrait’s shape (fallback 1:1).
seedinteger——

Refused, not ignored: prompt, width, height, num_inference_steps, max_sequence_length, output_format, output_quality — sending one fails the call instead of being dropped.

Where it stops

  • A look is a recipe, not a brand shade: use it to compare directions, not to promise an exact product.
  • The palette is matched to this person’s undertone and the original lighting, so the same reference gives a different result on another photo.

Try a look in the studio

A worked request for cutout-fast: { "model": "cutout-fast", "image_ids": [ "<file_id>" ] } submitted to POST /v1/tasks/alphanet-flux, polled at GET /v1/tasks/{task_id}, results read at GET /v1/tasks/{task_id}/result.

Output shapes for the four productised models

Omitted, aspect follows the first reference image instead of forcing a square: 1:1 = 1024 × 1024 · 3:4 = 768 × 1024 · 4:3 = 1024 × 768 · 2:3 = 768 × 1152 · 3:2 = 1152 × 768 · 16:9 = 1344 × 768 · 9:16 = 768 × 1344.

For a machine

The whole catalog is at /api-catalog.json, one model per file at /api-catalog/<model>.json. Model names are frozen: they are billing-visible, so renaming one is a breaking change.

DLSS5NVIDIA / Erase Object

AI image tool

Erase Object

Name what should go: the model removes it and rebuilds the surface underneath, keeping the rest of the frame as it was.

DLSS5NVIDIA is an independent browser-based DLSS 5-style effect converter, online visual enhancer and AI image generator for creating visual references from uploaded game frames and character images. It keeps structure, pose and identity as reviewable constraints while changing style, lighting and materials, and also offers separate upscale and restoration workflows. It is not an official NVIDIA DLSS runtime.

Erase an object →

JPG, PNG and WebP · up to 10 MiB · 1024 × 1024 PNG output, about a minute

What is Erase Object?

Erase Object is a browser-based object erasing workflow for people who already have a source image and need a controlled visual change. It uses a task-specific instruction rather than a blank prompt, so the requested output starts from the existing composition, subject or material. The page's before-and-after example is an illustrative reference; the result from your own file depends on its resolution, lighting, crop and visible detail.

How the workflow works

The workflow has three decisions. First, choose the largest original file instead of a screenshot or a second-generation social download. Next, confirm what is allowed to change and what must remain anchored: the task prompt is written for object erasing, while the page shows the applicable input and output limits before submission. Finally, compare the source and result at 100 percent and download only after the information-sensitive areas pass your review. This order matters because a plausible AI result can look polished while still changing a face, label, edge or background.

Input, output and source quality

Use a clear JPG, PNG or WebP with enough pixels for the details you care about. For this page, the published intake note is: JPG, PNG and WebP · up to 10 MiB · 1024 × 1024 PNG output, about a minute. A clean input gives the model stronger evidence about edges, colour and texture. If the source is already heavily compressed, crop it tightly or find the original before spending a credit. Keep the source file beside the output; the service is an enhancement estimate, not a reversible edit history.

When to use this tool

  • Objects that spoil a photo
  • Watermarks and logos on your own images
  • Text and labels you no longer need
  • Repair work on old photos

How it works

  1. Choose your image — Select a JPG, PNG or WebP up to 10 MiB — any pixel size, since the reference is scaled to the model before it renders. Photos with one obvious object work best.
  2. Name what should go — Describe the object to remove in the studio, then submit. The task takes about a minute and uses 1 credit.
  3. Compare and download — Check where the object was and the rest of the frame, then download the 1024 × 1024 PNG.

When this workflow fits

This workflow is a good fit for Objects that spoil a photo, Watermarks and logos on your own images, Text and labels you no longer need, Repair work on old photos. It is especially useful when the subject is already recognizable and the job is to remove an object from it while preserving the scene's main structure. It is less useful when the source has no recoverable detail, when the requested change is an exact measurement, or when the output will be used as an official record. In those cases, use the original capture, a design or editing application, or the receiving authority's own specification.

Limits and responsible use

Best for an object on a textured or continuous surface — a table, a wall, a floor, sky or grass. The model rebuilds the covered area, so the result is a re-render, not a perfect copy of what was there. Because the whole frame is re-rendered, fine text and small details elsewhere in the photo can change slightly. Review the result at 100% before you rely on it. The service cannot guarantee that a small character, logo, number, face or repeated pattern will remain unchanged. A larger output also does not create new factual evidence; it creates a more usable visual estimate.

Credits and delivery

Your allowance and the task cost are shown before a signed-in job starts. The public example is available for comparison, while processing a personal file uses the displayed credit amount. A failed generation on our side is handled by the account workflow according to the billing policy. Check the output target and the source dimensions first so a task is not spent on a size you cannot use. For batch or API work, compare the per-image cost with storage, retries and your own review time.

A practical quality review

Before publishing, compare the result with the original in a fixed order: overall composition, subject identity, long straight edges, small text or labels, repeated texture, colour and shadows. Zooming to 100 percent exposes halos and invented marks that a thumbnail hides. For portraits, check eyes, teeth, hairline and skin texture. For products or architecture, check logos, windows, perspective and material boundaries. For generated edits, check that the requested change is present without unrelated objects or background drift.

Frequently asked questions

Does it work on watermarks and text?

Read the answer

Yes, as long as you own the image: describe the watermark or the line of text as the thing to remove. Dense or semi-transparent text over a busy background is the hardest case.

Why does the output come back at 1024 × 1024?

Read the answer

The model rebuilds the entire frame rather than patching pixels, and it works at a fixed 1024 px square. A larger original is therefore re-rendered at that size.

How long does an erase take?

Read the answer

About a minute on the shared GPUs behind this site. The task is queued if the hardware is busy, and a confirmed failure is refunded automatically.

Is there a size limit on the image I upload?

Read the answer

Only one here: the file is capped at 10 MiB, with no pixel ceiling — the reference image is scaled down inside the service before the frame is re-rendered at 1024 × 1024. (The other tools in the studio also cap the picture at 16 megapixels.)

AI Portrait Retouch

Clean up a portrait without asking for a new face. Choose a restrained retouch level and compare skin texture, eyes, hair and expression against the source.

DLSS5NVIDIA is an independent browser-based DLSS 5-style effect converter, online visual enhancer and AI image generator for creating visual references from uploaded game frames and character images. It keeps structure, pose and identity as reviewable constraints while changing style, lighting and materials, and also offers separate upscale and restoration workflows. It is not an official NVIDIA DLSS runtime.

Open portrait retouch →

One portrait · light, natural or magazine level · about a minute · 1 credit

What is AI Portrait Retouch?

AI Portrait Retouch is a browser-based portrait retouching workflow for people who already have a source image and need a controlled visual change. It uses a task-specific instruction rather than a blank prompt, so the requested output starts from the existing composition, subject or material. The page's before-and-after example is an illustrative reference; the result from your own file depends on its resolution, lighting, crop and visible detail.

How the workflow works

The workflow has three decisions. First, choose the largest original file instead of a screenshot or a second-generation social download. Next, confirm what is allowed to change and what must remain anchored: the task prompt is written for portrait retouching, while the page shows the applicable input and output limits before submission. Finally, compare the source and result at 100 percent and download only after the information-sensitive areas pass your review. This order matters because a plausible AI result can look polished while still changing a face, label, edge or background.

Input, output and source quality

Use a clear JPG, PNG or WebP with enough pixels for the details you care about. For this page, the published intake note is: One portrait · light, natural or magazine level · about a minute · 1 credit. A clean input gives the model stronger evidence about edges, colour and texture. If the source is already heavily compressed, crop it tightly or find the original before spending a credit. Keep the source file beside the output; the service is an enhancement estimate, not a reversible edit history.

When to use this tool

  • Profile photos
  • Creator portraits
  • Portrait portfolio drafts
  • Social image cleanup

How it works

  1. Choose a portrait — Upload a clear portrait with the face visible. The largest original file gives the model more useful texture to work with.
  2. Pick a level — Choose light, natural or magazine. Natural is the default when you want skin grain and face shape to remain believable.
  3. Review identity details — Compare the eyes, jawline, expression, hair and skin texture before downloading the result.

When this workflow fits

This workflow is a good fit for Profile photos, Creator portraits, Portrait portfolio drafts, Social image cleanup. It is especially useful when the subject is already recognizable and the job is to refine it while preserving the scene's main structure. It is less useful when the source has no recoverable detail, when the requested change is an exact measurement, or when the output will be used as an official record. In those cases, use the original capture, a design or editing application, or the receiving authority's own specification.

Limits and responsible use

Choose natural retouch when identity and skin texture matter. Use the strongest level only for a deliberate editorial look and always compare the eyes, jawline and expression with the source. Retouching can change facial detail even when the workflow asks to preserve identity. Do not use the result for biometric, legal or identity verification purposes. The service cannot guarantee that a small character, logo, number, face or repeated pattern will remain unchanged. A larger output also does not create new factual evidence; it creates a more usable visual estimate.

Credits and delivery

Your allowance and the task cost are shown before a signed-in job starts. The public example is available for comparison, while processing a personal file uses the displayed credit amount. A failed generation on our side is handled by the account workflow according to the billing policy. Check the output target and the source dimensions first so a task is not spent on a size you cannot use. For batch or API work, compare the per-image cost with storage, retries and your own review time.

A practical quality review

Before publishing, compare the result with the original in a fixed order: overall composition, subject identity, long straight edges, small text or labels, repeated texture, colour and shadows. Zooming to 100 percent exposes halos and invented marks that a thumbnail hides. For portraits, check eyes, teeth, hairline and skin texture. For products or architecture, check logos, windows, perspective and material boundaries. For generated edits, check that the requested change is present without unrelated objects or background drift.

Frequently asked questions

Will portrait retouch change my face?

Read the answer

The workflow asks the model to preserve identity, face shape and expression, but generative editing can still change details. Review the result before publishing.

Which retouch level should I choose?

Read the answer

Light is best for small blemishes, natural balances skin and eyes while keeping texture, and magazine is a stronger editorial finish. Start with natural.

Can I use the result for an ID document?

Read the answer

No. Do not use generative retouching for identity verification, passports, legal records or biometric decisions.
