Source image and style reference: give a room redraw a visual direction

A source image and style reference let you describe a room transformation with both an existing space and a desired visual language. Use the first to judge what should remain, and the second to discuss palette, materials, and atmosphere.

style conversion · neural redraw

A source image and style reference let you describe a room transformation with both an existing space and a desired visual language. Use the first to judge what should remain, and the second to discuss palette, materials, and atmosphere.

TL;DR

  • The room source supplies the space you intend to reinterpret; the reference supplies a visual direction.
  • The current room tool uses named style and room settings, with an optional extra instruction, rather than an unrestricted prompt box.
  • The existing FAQ warns that geometry can drift. It does not publish a guaranteed prompt-versus-reference priority rule.
  • The historical example below changes architecture. Our new submission remains queued and is not represented as another successful result.

Why this belongs to style conversion

A room redraw can turn a photograph into a concept for a different material and lighting treatment. The creative question is how the room might read under that direction. The result helps someone discuss a visual intention, while the photograph remains available to check what was changed along the way.

Our interior-design page is the relevant starting point because the actual samples are interiors. This is the A line of DLSS 5-style conversion and neural-render redraw. Studio is a delivery form; the transformation itself is the subject of this article.

The second image makes a brief more concrete when words such as warm, restrained, or natural could describe very different rooms. It may convey relationships between wood, fabric, wall color, and light. It should not be treated as a hidden specification for dimensions, a furniture shopping list, or an instruction to replace the photographed architecture.

Give the two images different jobs

The source establishes the room to review

Look at the first image before choosing a reference. Identify the wall openings, camera direction, ceiling line, and usable floor area. These become preservation criteria. If the output later changes them, a pleasing color treatment does not cancel the discrepancy.

The site's input below is an empty room with a door on the rear wall, a dark opening beside it, and visible equipment on the floor. Those observations are sufficient for comparing structure. We have not measured the room or inferred dimensions from the photograph.

The reference communicates the treatment

The second image shows a furnished interior with woven pendant shades, a grey sofa, light-colored textiles, plants, and wood surfaces. A reviewer can point to those features instead of assuming that a style name carries the same meaning for everyone involved.

Assigning that role does not prove the model will respect its limits. The site's showcase describes the second reference as guidance for palette and materials. That is the intended workflow, not a physical constraint on generation. The output still needs comparison against the source room.

What the text controls actually do here

The current interior workflow accepts a named style and a room type. In our submitted request these were Japandi and living room. The implementation can also append an optional extra instruction to its fixed brief. We left that optional field absent, so we cannot report an experiment about its strength.

This distinction matters when discussing prompts. A general image editor may expose a free-form prompt, but the specific room interface supplies structured choices. Saying that we typed a long custom prompt into this run would misdescribe the experiment. The recorded request contains only the fields that were actually submitted.

Text tells the workflow which direction or constraint the user wants to express. A reference image supplies visual content that can make a direction less ambiguous. Those are complementary roles in a brief; they are not measured weights, and we have no slider value or formula that establishes how much either one controls this model.

For general background, BFL's image-editing documentation discusses editing with textual and image inputs. Its multi-reference explanation describes combining reference content. These sources explain the broader concept, not the exact conflict behavior of the site's room model.

If text and reference disagree, what wins?

The checked interior FAQ does not specify a winner. Its relevant answer says the workflow requests preservation of room geometry, while warning that generative results may drift and asking the reader to review openings, straight lines, and perspective. We cannot turn that answer into a guarantee that text always wins or that the second image always wins.

For example, the presence of an arch in a reference should not be read as permission to claim that the source room has one. If the generated room introduces that arch, compare it against the source and the intended brief. The result may remain a mood reference while failing the requirement to preserve the photographed space.

As an editorial practice, resolve contradictory requirements before accepting an image. Write down which architectural features must remain and which visual features are inspirations. This is a review recommendation, not a newly invented model priority rule or a claim that we tested every conflicting combination.

What the historical example actually shows

The site's stored showcase links these two inputs to a Japandi output and records the named choices. We copied that existing output below. We do not label it as the result of today's queued request, and we do not repeat the showcase's timing or dimension fields as freshly measured facts.

The output visibly adopts furnishings and a material mood related to the reference. It also shows a large left window and an arched opening on the right, unlike the rear-door arrangement in the source. That difference prevents us from presenting the pair as a successful geometry-preserving transformation.

The original showcase description is more confident about preserved architecture than this visual comparison supports. We retain the source record but do not repeat that assertion as our conclusion. Looking at the actual pair is precisely why a source image and style reference should travel with the resulting concept.

Reproduce the steps that were actually performed

  1. Copy the site's room and style-reference files into separate, clearly named inputs; our exact copies and hashes are included.
  2. Upload the room first and the style image second to the existing interior-quality workflow.
  3. Submit the recorded style and room type. Our request uses japandi and living_room, with no custom prompt, seed, or output dimensions.
  4. Save the task identifier and inspect its status. The last saved status for this new task is QUEUED; it supplies no completed output for review.
  5. Separately open the historical input, reference, and output together to inspect the differences described above.

The request record substitutes local filenames for uploaded image identifiers so the role and order remain understandable without presenting temporary upload references as durable assets. The task record preserves the actual job identifier. Repeating an authenticated submission may consume service credits and cannot promise identical output.

We also ran the existing content-library capture script on a local inspection page containing the stored images. Its actual execution log and file manifest accompany the package. That replay reproduces a comparison surface; it neither advances the queued job nor manufactures a successful generation record.

Hand over the useful parts of the concept

For a room presentation, state what the image contributes: perhaps the relationship between muted walls and woven lighting, or the appearance of natural materials together. Keep the source room nearby and name any architectural departures. The recipient can then use the concept without mistaking it for a proposed measured layout.

A source image and style reference are also useful evidence when a result goes wrong. They let another reviewer see whether a disputed feature belonged to the original space, the inspiration image, or the generated interpretation. Without those inputs, a correction request can become a debate about an undocumented intention.

This example says nothing about commercially usable clothing replacement or face replacement. It contains no identity test. If your own authorized images include a person, review the face and identity with that person before accepting the result; a successful-looking room conversion would provide no evidence about that separate task.

Limits and independence

This workflow cannot certify dimensions, unchanged architecture, furniture fit, identity, commercial suitability, or a universal prompt-reference precedence rule. The FAQ's concept-versus-measurement boundary remains applicable. We operate the linked site and are independent of NVIDIA, AMD, and Black Forest Labs. These are site-owned samples for static style-conversion discussion, not NVIDIA runtime screenshots or third-party product test images.

NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 and the practical question behind 4K upscaling

Broadcast lab: Reports describing 4k video upscaling and frame-generation features are useful only when the image workflow is shown separately. This article gives a controlled answer with a site-owned pair and a manifest that another reader can inspect.

image workflow · entry-point

Broadcast lab: Reports describing 4k video upscaling and frame-generation features are useful only when the image workflow is shown separately. This article gives a controlled answer with a site-owned pair and a manifest that another reader can inspect.

Our main workflow is style conversion into DLSS 5-style visual references, delivered through the DLSS 5 Studio desktop app. The image-quality inspection prompted by this Broadcast report covers only a limited entry point for poor-quality existing pictures; it does not define the product or demonstrate its style-conversion capability.

TL;DR

  • Broadcast coverage is context; the image pair is the check.
  • Keep the original frame beside the processed frame.
  • Record the operation and export fields.
  • Do not turn a Broadcast discussion into a Broadcast benchmark.

What the linked coverage does and does not say

Broadcast lab: The search phrase NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 4K upscaling points to a practical question: what can a person check after a feed, export, or tool has softened a reference? Our answer starts with the file, not with a vendor promise.

Broadcast lab: The public landing page is /image-upscaler, where the browser path is labeled as an independent visual workflow. The page is not a driver download and it does not claim to be a product from the company named in Broadcast coverage.

Broadcast lab: The first source is NVIDIA Broadcast product information (https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/broadcasting/broadcast-app/). It provides context for broadcast coverage, while our sample files provide the evidence for the image-handling steps.

Broadcast lab: The second source is NVIDIA newsroom (https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/). It is linked so a reader can check the surrounding report or product material instead of relying on a paraphrase in this article.

The input is the evidence

Broadcast lab: A current headline can explain why broadcast coverage is being searched, but the headline is not an image license. We use site-owned files and retain their original filenames so the visual pair has a clear provenance.

Broadcast lab: For this angle, the most revealing crop is not a dramatic skyline or a logo. It is an ordinary edge: a building line, a product contour, or a small region where compression turns a smooth boundary into blocks.

Broadcast lab: Open the low-resolution input first. Read a few characters, look at the repeated texture, and note where your eyes stop trusting the picture. That observation is part of the record before any enhancement step is run.

Broadcast lab: Run the browser sample once and keep the resulting file beside the input. Do not replace the input halfway through the comparison, because a different source makes NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 4K upscaling impossible to reproduce as a check.

A reproducible run

Broadcast lab: Use the same displayed width for both files. A larger result can look more impressive simply because it occupies more pixels, so the comparison needs a stable viewing frame and a caption that names the two files.

Broadcast lab: Record the operation, input dimensions, output dimensions, and date. We do not fill an absent field with an estimate. A missing setting is a limitation to report, not a reason to invent a number.

Broadcast lab: If a face, sign, or label changes meaning, keep the original as the decision reference. The visual-enhancer step can make an edge easier to inspect, yet it cannot recover ground truth that was not present in reports describing 4K video upscaling and frame-generation features.

Broadcast lab: For a developer, the useful artifact is a request manifest. It shows which endpoint the operator controls, which files were read, and where the output was written; it does not hide a provider key in a sample command.

Failure cases worth keeping

Broadcast lab: For a designer, the useful artifact is a side-by-side crop with a caption. The crop should reveal a concrete question such as whether a diagonal line is continuous or whether a repeated pattern has been softened.

Broadcast lab: For a researcher, the useful artifact is a repeatable condition. Keep the seed, prompt, tile size, export format, or node graph fixed when those fields exist. Change one condition only when the goal is to learn what caused a visual difference.

Broadcast lab: This is where NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 4K upscaling becomes a workflow term rather than a slogan. The phrase names a task people can try, while the article records what happened in one controlled sample and what remained unknown.

The accompanying captions say what is visible, so the image pair is not asked to carry a silent performance claim or a hidden comparison.

A practical handoff

Broadcast lab: This page does not provide a command-line tool. The example command sends only to an endpoint the operator controls. It does not require our hosted credits and it does not pretend to reproduce a vendor benchmark.

Broadcast lab: If you want to test a personal image, use only a file you have permission to process. Keep client material local when the client has not agreed to an upload, and preserve the untouched source for later review.

Broadcast lab: The durable lesson from broadcast coverage is therefore modest: make the transformation visible, make the source traceable, and write down the failure case. That is more useful than claiming a universal result from one attractive crop.

Broadcast lab: Readers can follow the numbered procedure below, then open the image-upscaler page for a cached example. The online path and the separate desktop request path have different availability and should not be merged in the copy.

Reproduction command

curl -X POST https://your-endpoint.example/enhance -F image=@broadcast-input.jpg -o broadcast-output.jpg

Sources and disclosure

Broadcast lab: This independent project is not affiliated with NVIDIA, Adobe, Tesla, Topaz Labs, or ComfyUI. The names are used to identify the subject of the linked sources; they do not imply endorsement, sponsorship, or shared ownership.

Broadcast lab: The boundary is explicit: this article does not publish frame rates, does not promise a fixed quality change, and does not turn a visual pair into a hardware test. It documents an inspectable image operation.

Broadcast-specific checklist

Broadcast lab: Broadcast coverage often mixes webcam, video, and game language. Separate those contexts before testing an image. A still frame exported from a video can carry motion blur and compression that were never part of the original scene. The sample here is a still-image check, so it should not be presented as a live Broadcast measurement.

Crimson Desert PC Optimization Guide: DLSS 4.5, FSR 4, and Getting 60fps at 4K (2026)

Crimson Desert PC Optimization Guide: DLSS 4.5, FSR 4, and Getting 60fps at 4K (2026)

crimson desert · crimson desert dlss · crimson desert performance · dlss 4.5 · 绯红荒漠优化

Crimson Desert launched on March 19, 2026, and immediately became one of the most visually ambitious open-world games in years. Here's how to get the most out of it.

Supported Upscaling Technologies

  • NVIDIA DLSS 4 (all RTX GPUs — upscaling + frame generation on RTX 40/50)
  • NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 (all RTX GPUs — note: DLSS 4.5 has a flickering bug at launch; DLSS 4 is more stable)
  • NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction (RTX 20 series and newer)
  • AMD FSR 3 (any GPU)
  • AMD FSR 4 (RDNA 4 only)
  • Apple MetalFX (Mac)

Important: Use DLSS 4 for stability until Pearl Abyss patches the DLSS 4.5 flickering issue.

Benchmark Targets by GPU (4K)

The table keeps the original comparison position, but replaces unsupported frame-rate claims with settings that a reader can reproduce. We do not publish FPS here because we have no matching local GPU run or citable first-party result.

GPU tier4K settings to tryUpscaling / frame-generation combinationFPS source
RTX 50 seriesUltra or CinematicDLSS 4 Quality; test frame generation separatelyRun your own capture with GPU, driver, resolution, preset and date recorded
RTX 4090 / 4080Ultra or HighDLSS 4 Quality or Balanced; test frame generation separatelyRun your own capture with GPU, driver, resolution, preset and date recorded
RX 9070 XTUltra or HighFSR 4 Quality; test frame generation separatelyRun your own capture with GPU, driver, resolution, preset and date recorded

We do not fill in FPS: there is no matching local measurement for these rows. Record the fields above if you run your own test.

Recommended Settings

High-End (RTX 5080/5090, RX 9070 XT) — 4K Ultra 60fps+

  • Quality: Ultra or Cinematic
  • Upscaling: DLSS 4 Quality mode (or FSR 4 Quality on AMD)
  • Frame Generation: Enable
  • Ray Reconstruction: Enable
  • Shadow Distance: Ultra
  • NPC Density: Ultra

Mid-High (RTX 4080, RTX 4070 Ti Super) — 4K High 60fps

  • Quality: High
  • Upscaling: DLSS 4 Balanced mode
  • Frame Generation: Enable
  • Volumetric Fog: Medium (saves 8-10% with minimal visual difference)

Mid-Range (RTX 4070, RTX 4060 Ti) — 1440p High 60fps+

  • Quality: High
  • Upscaling: DLSS 4 Quality mode
  • NPC Density: Medium (major improvement to 1% lows in Kastone)

The Stuttering Fix

Reduce NPC Density to Medium, lower Shadow Distance, and enable DLSS 4. Also ensure your drivers are up to date: NVIDIA 581.29+ or AMD 25.9.2+.

Will Crimson Desert Get DLSS 5 Support?

DLSS 5 began shipping on 1 September 2026 with NBA 2K27. Crimson Desert is not currently on the confirmed DLSS 5 title list. However, given Pearl Abyss's deep integration with NVIDIA, DLSS 5 support in a future patch is plausible.

DLSS 5 Online Image Upscaler: What Works in a Browser?

A practical guide to browser-based DLSS 5-style conversion and AI image upscaling, including input preparation, comparison checks and what an online tool can and cannot recover.

dlss 5 online · ai image upscaler · 4k upscaling · neural super resolution

DLSS and browser-based AI upscaling are different tools

NVIDIA DLSS is an in-game rendering technology tied to supported RTX hardware. A browser-based AI upscaler processes uploaded images on a server, so it can work from a phone, Mac, or PC without an RTX card.

What an online upscaler can do

It can enlarge a photo, recover apparent detail, reduce softness, and produce a higher-resolution image for review or download. Results depend on the source image and the model; AI cannot recover information that was never captured.

A simple workflow

  1. Upload a JPEG, PNG, or WebP.
  2. Choose the requested enhancement or style.
  3. Compare the input and output.
  4. Download only after checking faces, text, edges, and repeated patterns.

This site is an independent, non-official showcase inspired by neural super-resolution concepts and is not an NVIDIA product.

Seedance 2.5 + Video Super-Resolution: A Lower-Cost 4K Workflow (2026)

A source-led cost study of generating Seedance 2.5 clips at a lower resolution and finishing them with video super-resolution instead of paying for every native high-resolution render.

seedance 2.5 · video super resolution · video upscaling · 4k video · ai video cost · BytePlus · RealESRGAN

Seedance 2.5 is interesting for a reason that goes beyond a better demo reel: it can move a video workflow from “generate a short clip” toward “finish a small production.” ByteDance says the model can generate up to 30 seconds in one pass, extend a sequence in multiple rounds, accept up to 30 images, 10 video clips, and 10 audio clips as references, and perform timestamp-level and reference-based edits. The model is available on consumer products first, with API access through BytePlus ModelArk.

One implementation detail matters before comparing costs: BytePlus's current video API page lists Seedance 2.5 ('dreamina-seedance-2-5-260628') at 480p and 720p, 24 fps, and 4–30 seconds. It does not list native 4K output for that API route. Some consumer products and third-party gateways expose different options, so a 4K claim must be checked against the exact provider and model ID. For DLSS5, video super-resolution is therefore a delivery extension of the official low-resolution route, not a claim that the official 2.5 API itself renders native 4K.

The practical question for a production tool is not whether provider-native high resolution looks good. It is whether every iteration needs to be rendered at the final delivery resolution. For prompt exploration, story blocking, social previews, and many AI-generated shots, a lower-resolution Seedance render followed by video super-resolution can reduce the cost of failed iterations.

The two workflows

Provider-native high-resolution generation asks the selected provider to produce the final delivery size in one generation. It is the safer choice when small text, hair, thin lines, fast motion, or exact texture fidelity must survive the first render.

Generate low, then upscale uses Seedance 2.5 for motion, composition, audio, and story control at 480p or 720p. A video super-resolution model then processes the finished clip frame by frame and exports 1080p or 4K. This separates creative iteration from delivery finishing.

WorkflowBest useMain cost driverMain risk
Provider-native high-resolutionFinal hero shots, text-heavy scenes, client delivery when the route supports itProvider output tokens and resolutionMore expensive retries
480p/720p + video super-resolutionDrafts, social clips, catalog video, repeated experimentsSeedance generation plus output megapixelsFlicker or invented detail during upscaling

A transparent cost estimate

Public BytePlus references price Seedance 2.5 by resolution and generated tokens. An independent public tracker has normalized the 480p and 720p text-to-video examples to roughly $0.103 per second and $0.231 per second respectively; the live ModelArk rate card should be treated as the source of truth because pricing and promotions can change. A five-second clip therefore starts around $0.52 at 480p or $1.16 at 720p before any finishing step. These figures compare the official low-resolution API route; they are not an official Seedance 2.5 4K price.

The fal.ai video-upscaler endpoint publishes a rate of $0.0008 per output megapixel and uses RealESRGAN on each frame. At 24 fps, a five-second 4K output is about 995 megapixels of processed frames, or roughly $0.80 for the super-resolution step. That gives an illustrative budget:

Five-second outputSeedance generation4K super-resolutionEstimated total
480p → 4K$0.52$0.80$1.32
720p → 4K$1.16$0.80$1.96

These are planning estimates, not a promise of a final invoice. They exclude storage, transfer, retries, audio or reference-video input charges, and our service margin. The useful product insight is the break-even rule: if a native high-resolution attempt costs more than the low-resolution render plus the super-resolution pass, the two-step path is cheaper; if quality failures force a re-render, the apparent saving disappears.

Where the two-step path wins

It is a strong fit for short-form social content, product teasers, motion mood boards, real-estate fly-throughs, game-concept clips, and internal review. The user can iterate on prompt, camera movement, references, and timing at a lower cost, then pay for the finishing pass only once.

It is a weaker fit for tiny typography, UI capture, dense crowds, rapid cuts, heavy film grain, and shots where identity or texture must remain pixel-accurate. A frame-by-frame upscaler can create plausible detail while changing it over time. We should show a side-by-side preview and label the result as AI-enhanced rather than promising native 4K fidelity.

How DLSS5 NVIDIA should ship it

The first release should be a Seedance 2.5 video workflow, not a generic “make any video 4K” button:

  • Generate a preview at 480p or 720p with duration and aspect-ratio controls.
  • Offer a clear “Finish in 1080p” or “Finish in 4K” step after the preview is accepted.
  • Show the estimated credits before the job starts, including separate generation and super-resolution costs.
  • Keep provider keys on the server and route the job through a provider adapter so BytePlus, fal, or our Alphanet service can be swapped without changing the UI.
  • Deduct credits atomically per stage and refund the failed stage. Do not charge for a super-resolution job that never starts.
  • Store the original preview and final output separately, with signed download URLs and an expiry policy.

The backend job graph is simple: 'seedance.generate → normalize video → video.superres → persist result → notify client'. Each stage needs an idempotency key, a provider job ID, a cost estimate, and a final measured cost. This lets us compare estimated versus actual spend before setting public prices.

Our recommendation

Ship the two-step workflow first and market it honestly as a cost-aware 4K finishing pipeline. Use low resolution for exploration, reserve native high resolution for shots that need it, and let the user choose. The feature creates value because it combines Seedance 2.5’s stronger story and reference control with a cheaper finishing path; it does not pretend that super-resolution is identical to native generation.

Reading an Aiarty image enhancer review: reproduce the comparison before trusting the detail

Keep the input, record the settings, and inspect matching regions before accepting an enhancement claim. A convincing after image can demonstrate a useful edit without proving that missing detail was recovered.

image workflow · entry-point

Keep the input, record the settings, and inspect matching regions before accepting an enhancement claim. A convincing after image can demonstrate a useful edit without proving that missing detail was recovered.

DLSS 5 Studio turns existing images into DLSS 5-style visual references through style conversion and neural-render redraw, with the desktop app as the handover. This review-method article covers only a limited entry point for poor-quality existing pictures; its kitchen example leads back to room style conversion, not a claim that sharpening is the product.

TL;DR

  • Save original bytes, output bytes, settings, and provenance.
  • Separate an attractive redraw from a reconstruction supported by a reference.
  • Inspect edges, texture, text, and identity independently.
  • Our demonstration retrieves a cached kitchen redraw; it is not an Aiarty test.

Keep these notes with the files

  • Input record: file hash, ownership, and whether a reference exists.
  • Operation record: prompt, parameters, cache state, and returned file.
  • Observation record: named regions, visible changes, and unresolved questions.

What prompted this guide

RedShark published its Aiarty article on October 15, 2026, with a Sponsored Article label. That disclosure matters when deciding what kind of evidence the page supplies. We use the article as the reason to discuss comparison methods, without repeating its pricing or performance claims. Read the RedShark article.

Someone searching for an aiarty image enhancer review may want to know whether a beautiful comparison will transfer to their own archive. The useful next step is a small, documented experiment. We have not installed or benchmarked Aiarty, and this guide offers no verdict on its quality. Its user guide is a separate reference for readers who choose to test that product themselves.

Do not infer the ownership of every comparison image from the sponsorship label alone. What matters for your experiment is whether you have the original input, permission to use it, and enough settings to repeat the operation. A web preview without those pieces cannot settle how your photograph will behave.

Start by naming the actual operation

Our own public kitchen example accepts an existing render and asks for a photographic interpretation while keeping the layout. On October 23 we requested that example and received a successful response marked cached: true. We downloaded the input and the stored output, then captured a local inspection page containing both files.

That record establishes a real, repeatable retrieval and a real pair to inspect. It does not establish a fresh inference run, a deblurring result, or a measured restoration score. The input is an interior render, not a deliberately blurred camera original. Those distinctions belong beside the image, where readers will encounter them.

Look for changes the prompt did not make obvious

The pair preserves a recognizable kitchen arrangement, but lighting and surface appearance differ. The input includes a small interface overlay near the upper edge; that overlay is absent in the output. This is a concrete reason to inspect the whole frame even when the intended task sounds limited.

A cleaner-looking wall can be desirable in an illustration. The same change would matter differently in a documented screenshot. Decide which content is allowed to change before seeing the output, so that an appealing result does not quietly rewrite the acceptance criteria.

A reproducible retrieval you can perform

The following commands require curl and a shell. Run them from a new working directory. They request the same public example and preserve the response before downloading the result. No Aiarty installation or account credential is involved.

curl --fail --silent --show-error \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"sample":"sample1"}' \
  https://www.dlss5nvidia.com/api/image-edit/samples -o run.json
curl --fail --silent --show-error \
  https://www.dlss5nvidia.com/examples/sample1.jpg -o input.jpg
curl --fail --silent --show-error \
  'https://www.dlss5nvidia.com/api/image-edit/samples?sample=sample1' -o result.webp

Read the response before drawing conclusions. Our response states the prompt, the input path, the result path, and the cache flag. If your response is an error or indicates that processing is still underway, stop and record that condition. Do not rename an error document as an image or borrow an unrelated result.

The shipped assets include our response and SHA-256 hashes. A later cache revision could produce different bytes. Matching hashes confirm that you inspected our exact files; different hashes mean you should record a new version of the example. Neither outcome measures whether the model recovers truth.

Keep a reference separate from the input

For a restoration experiment, start with a photograph you own and retain an untouched reference. Make a degraded working copy through a recorded blur, resize, or compression operation. Process only that working copy. Then compare the output with the untouched reference, using the same region and display size.

This controlled exercise asks whether known detail survives a specific degradation and processing chain. An old family scan without an original reference asks a narrower question: whether the edit is useful and whether visible contradictions appear. It cannot reveal every invented feature, because the missing evidence is unavailable.

Four inspection passes that answer different questions

Edges and geometry

Follow a cabinet seam from one end to the other. Check whether it stays connected, changes direction, doubles, or disappears behind an invented highlight. Inspect the corners of the window and the outline of the tap. Record the location and the change, rather than writing that the entire picture became sharper.

A halo may make an edge easier to notice while also changing its profile. At fit-to-window size, that may look persuasive. At a matched crop, you can judge whether the transition remains acceptable for the intended use. The appropriate conclusion concerns that edge and that display size.

Texture and material

Wood grain is a useful trap for an incautious reviewer. A generated pattern can look plausible while having no correspondence with the input. Look for repeated marks and large changes in direction. Compare the pattern with a real reference if you have one; otherwise describe it as a new surface interpretation.

The same reasoning applies to hair, fabric, grass, and brick. Their familiar structure makes added detail easy to believe. A texture that feels natural supports an aesthetic judgment, but it does not identify the texture that was present when the source was made.

Text and symbols

Read labels character by character against the input. A mark that becomes legible only after generation should remain unverified unless an independent source confirms it. Do not use visual confidence as a transcription method. A realistic-looking serial number can be more misleading than an unreadable original.

Our kitchen scene contains small appliance markings, but we do not claim to recover their wording. That is an intentional limit on interpretation. If your actual task concerns text, choose a source with known wording and keep the acceptance rule strict: changed characters are an error even when the label looks cleaner.

Faces and identity

This sample contains no face, so it provides no evidence about identity preservation. For your own authorized portrait test, inspect eye shape, eyelids, teeth, hairline, and distinctive marks separately. Keep a reference photograph available and ask the person pictured to review edits intended for personal use.

Do not combine these checks into a single beauty score. Someone can prefer the expression while noticing that a distinctive feature has changed. Report both observations. The absence of an obvious error also does not establish that every reconstructed detail is accurate.

Write a result that another reader can audit

A useful note names the task, input, settings, output, inspected regions, and unresolved questions. It distinguishes observation from inference. For our pair, the disappearance of the input overlay is visible; the exact cause of that change inside the model is not established by the files.

Keep failed and ordinary attempts alongside the chosen example. If you select one attractive output from several trials, disclose the selection. If there was only one retrieved cache entry, say that instead. A reader should be able to distinguish a curated illustration from a repeatability experiment.

When reading an aiarty image enhancer review, use the same checklist without demanding that a promotional illustration answer every scientific question. Ask what evidence it actually supplies. A downloadable input supports reproduction; a matching reference supports fidelity checks; a screenshot alone supports a more limited visual inspection.

Try the method on a relevant image

The unblur image page is a starting point for inspecting a soft image of your own. Keep the original and decide whether the goal is readability, presentation, or preservation before processing. Stop if a result changes content that your use requires you to retain.

Our enhancement configuration uses flux-klein to redraw an image, offers target factors of 2× and 4×, and caps each output edge at 1536 pixels with dimensions aligned to multiples of 16. The requested factor can be reduced by that cap. This sample's cached style-conversion request is a separate operation, not a demonstration that those factors were achieved.

A fresh enhancement check alongside the cached example

We also ran the compressed screenshot of this inspection page through flux-klein during this batch. The exact input and completed output are included here; this is the same documented run discussed from a sharing perspective in the companion article. It is not another independent trial.

The request and result records let you audit which file was processed. To repeat the check with authorized model access, upload the included compressed JPEG and use the prompt and settings in assets/enhance-request.json; preserve your returned bytes separately. Read the heading against the input before assessing texture. In our saved output, lettering changes, so the result fails an exact-text preservation requirement even if someone prefers its surfaces.

Boundaries and independence

We cannot establish Aiarty's quality from this exercise, recover unseen historical detail, or promise facial reconstruction. The kitchen pair demonstrates a documented redraw and an inspection method; it is not a pixel-exact restoration benchmark. We publish this guide for our own site's readers, so the landing-page link serves our product. We are independent and not affiliated with NVIDIA, AMD, Aiarty, or RedShark.

A neural redraw checklist: use style conversion without losing track of what changed

Style conversion can make another lighting and material direction visible from an existing image. Review small text, symbols, identity, and proportions separately so a useful visual reference does not silently become evidence for details the redraw changed.

style conversion · neural redraw

Style conversion can make another lighting and material direction visible from an existing image. Review small text, symbols, identity, and proportions separately so a useful visual reference does not silently become evidence for details the redraw changed.

TL;DR

  • Judge the intended visual direction and preservation requirements separately.
  • Keep complete sources and outputs, including failed or provisional results.
  • Inspect lettering, emblems, recognizable features, and spatial relationships before approval.
  • Our recorded room examples support observations about those images, not a universal fidelity claim.

Review the change you asked for

A neural redraw checklist starts with the creative task. In these examples the task was to reinterpret lighting and material appearance in existing interior renders. The purpose was to make a visual direction available for discussion while keeping the source arrangement available for comparison.

That is the A-line capability: DLSS 5-style conversion and neural-render redraw. The useful outcome might be a reference for daylight, indirect illumination, fabric response, or surface contrast. It is not defined by a desktop application's packaging, and it does not require pretending that the generated scene is a faithful photograph of a real room.

Our before-and-after page provides the relevant comparison context. This article adds a way to record which parts of a result remain suitable for reference and which parts must not be carried into a final design. A boundary note is useful when it changes that decision.

The records behind the pictures

The included room and kitchen pairs come from recorded site-owned flux-klein jobs dated October 21. Their original inputs, returned outputs, prompts, and task records are retained. We copied the existing comparisons without changing the light, color, or content to manufacture a stronger difference.

The historical review treated these as lighting-direction candidates with visible departures, not as approved geometric reconstructions. That status stays attached here. We did not rerun those model jobs for this article, and we do not turn a successful API status into a passed visual review.

The bedroom remains recognizable, while the bedding appearance, artwork, and some cabinet details differ. Those are specific places to inspect against the source. The room's broad familiarity does not establish exact preservation of a decorative motif or the relationship between furniture and the surrounding architecture.

Small text: compare meaning before appearance

Inspect characters as characters

A caption, appliance label, sign, or interface control communicates information. In a style redraw it can also become visual texture. The review must therefore ask whether the actual characters survived, not whether the mark looks sufficiently like writing from a normal viewing distance.

In the kitchen pair, the upper interface overlay and appliance labels remain available to inspect. We do not certify the wording of tiny text from the comparison image. Use the supplied full files and the source wording, if known, rather than treating plausible output lettering as a transcript.

If a letter cannot be verified, mark it unresolved. That is different from claiming that it definitely changed. If a clear source character becomes a different character, record the mismatch. A useful checklist distinguishes observed errors from places where the available image cannot support a judgment.

Keep annotations outside generated pixels

Write the task identifier and review decision in the surrounding document. If you place them inside an image and send that image through another redraw, they become part of the generated scene. The audit trail should remain readable independently of the model's treatment of text.

For a presentation, you can supply a separate caption describing the creative direction. Do not use an invented label in the image as evidence of a product name or a historical fact. A visual reference can still serve its purpose while the editor explicitly excludes its lettering from reuse.

Logos and symbols: shape alone is insufficient

A logo may remain recognizable while its letter spacing, internal cutouts, or proportions change. The same applies to a fictional emblem that a character designer wants preserved. Check the mark against the authorized source artwork, including the space around it, rather than approving it because the color is familiar.

Our room examples do not provide a verified brand-logo test. We include logo inspection as an acceptance criterion for readers whose own sources contain such marks. We do not invent a successful logo-preservation experiment from an appliance label that cannot be verified here.

A generated symbol also does not establish permission to use it commercially. The relevant practical step is to keep the source and ask the responsible owner or designer to approve the final mark where needed. This is an editorial review recommendation, not a legal determination.

Identity: familiarity needs a separate check

A recognizable person or character has more than a broad silhouette. Face shape, hairline, expression, distinctive marks, and costume construction can matter to recognition. A change that seems minor to the editor may be obvious to the person pictured or the character's designer.

These interior examples contain no faces. They cannot establish facial identity preservation, nor can they tell you how a face-oriented tool behaves. For an authorized portrait, compare against the original and seek the subject's review before treating the result as an acceptable representation.

Keep the identity question separate from whether the rendering looks attractive. You can like the light while rejecting a changed expression. For a fictional character, the same logic applies to a helmet, badge, hairstyle, or costume seam that carries the design's identity.

Exact proportions: a concept is not a measurement

A room can look credible while the apparent size of the bench, the placement of a cabinet seam, or the relation between window and wall changes. A plausible perspective does not prove that furniture fits. If a decision depends on dimensions, retain measured information outside the generated picture.

The bedroom record requests preservation of the arrangement. Its review nevertheless identifies changes in artwork, pillow patterns, cabinet layout, and some spatial proportions. The appropriate conclusion is that the image can inform a lighting discussion while remaining unsuitable as evidence of exact geometry.

Do not convert that observation into a percentage of geometric accuracy. We did not establish a calibrated camera, measured reference scene, or numerical registration experiment. The record supports a visual comparison and named concerns, which are sufficient to decide that a stricter geometry claim has not been demonstrated.

Repeat the inspection we actually performed

  1. Open room-run.json and kitchen-run.json to read the original task descriptions and successful completion records.
  2. View each complete source beside its returned output. The package retains separate input and output files as well as the comparison images.
  3. Check the bedroom artwork, bedding, and cabinet lines, then the kitchen overlay, tap, and appliance outlines.
  4. Separate direct observations from unverified text and untested face or logo behavior.
  5. Record whether each image remains useful as a visual-direction reference and which elements are excluded from reuse.

We also reused the library's reproduce-capture.mjs script on a local page containing the recorded comparisons. Its execution log and manifest are included. The procedure reproduces the inspection surface; it does not create a new inference result or simulate a successful preservation test.

Open assets/audit.html to inspect the same embedded comparisons. To rerun the browser capture, follow the environment instructions in assets/README.md and execute the supplied script from that directory. We ran that script for this package. Any new model experiment would require its own request and returned file, so it is outside this replay.

Write a decision someone else can use

A review note should name the intended visual change, the region checked, what was observed, and the permitted use. For the bedroom, a reader can discuss material response while retaining a concern about decorative and geometric differences. A generic approved stamp would discard that useful distinction.

For text, use separate outcomes such as verified against source, mismatch observed, and not readable enough to verify. For identity, distinguish a subject-approved result from an editor's impression. For proportions, distinguish a visual plausibility check from a measurement. These labels describe the evidence rather than pretending every task has the same threshold.

The neural redraw checklist is intended to keep useful creative work moving. A result that fails one requirement may still be an honest reference for another purpose, provided the recipient can see the limitation. Reclassifying the use is acceptable; hiding the failure is not a substitute for review.

Technical context and limits

BFL's image-editing guide describes prompt-based edits, and its multi-reference overview explains combining reference content. Those pages give background, not independent validation of these recorded outputs. No images from either source appear here.

Use this neural redraw checklist before calling an output a finished reference. It cannot guarantee unchanged words, logos, identity, proportions, commercial suitability, or temporal stability. This article concerns independent static style conversion, not NVIDIA runtime output. We operate the linked site and are not affiliated with NVIDIA, AMD, or Black Forest Labs. The original files remain the basis for every review.

DLSS 5-style game-frame redraws: inspect HUD and text before sharing

A game HUD carries instructions and state, not just decoration. In a DLSS 5-style still-image redraw, inspect those meanings against the source before sharing.

DLSS 5 · game character

A game HUD carries instructions and state, not just decoration. In a DLSS 5-style still-image redraw, inspect those meanings against the source before sharing. Our examples show scene markings, not a tested HUD; the six checks below are a review checklist.

TL;DR

  • A believable game character can sit beside unreadable or misleading interface elements. Review them separately.
  • Check health indicators, task text, crosshairs, menus, map cues and in-world labels before submission.
  • Treat a missing or illegible element as unresolved until you can compare it with a trustworthy source. Do not guess its intended content.
  • These are independent image-review recommendations. They do not diagnose NVIDIA DLSS 5 or promise faithful text generation.

Keep the runtime question separate from the illustration

NVIDIA's DLSS 5 research page describes a renderer-grounded system for games. This article concerns our separate still-image workflow and does not test that system. A changed sign in an independent redraw is not evidence that the official runtime changes a game's interface.

The connection is the game-frame subject and the need to respect authored information while discussing visual treatment. A frame may combine a character, environment, decorative lettering and actionable interface. Those parts need different acceptance criteria. Atmospheric success cannot certify that a number, a menu choice or an aiming cue remains correct.

There is also no sequence here. A still image cannot establish whether an indicator behaves properly during play, whether text flickers between frames or whether a crosshair follows an input. Do not label a visual comparison as a playability test. The limited question is whether a particular picture can be shared honestly for its stated purpose.

What the available pictures do and do not show

The site-owned source below contains a character on a neon street with sign-like marks in the environment. It does not provide a health bar, a task panel, a crosshair or a menu that we can use as HUD ground truth. It is useful for separating scene detail from claims about interface fidelity.

The historical result has more elaborate sign-like forms and a different head treatment. We can inspect their appearance, but the source does not establish the intended characters well enough to certify a literal transcription. Calling the result readable at a glance would not prove that it says the same thing.

This distinction prevents an attractive example from answering a question it never tested. We do not count a HUD failure in these pictures because the relevant elements are absent. We also do not count a pass. For missing evidence, the appropriate entry is not assessed, rather than a reassuring default.

Six places to inspect before submission

The following checks are potential failure categories and acceptance questions. They are not six failures measured in the illustrated pair, and the order is a review sequence rather than a statistical ranking of what models damage most often.

1. Health, stamina and other state bars

Compare the indicator's length, segmentation, labels and color relationship with the source. A redraw that rounds the end, merges divisions or changes the apparent fill could communicate a different state even if it still resembles a polished interface. These are examples of changes to look for, not observed events in our sample.

Do not infer the exact value from a bar whose source is unclear. If an accompanying number is visible, check the number independently from the shape. A decorative red strip in the scene is not automatically a health bar, so identify the element before judging whether it was retained.

2. Mission, dialogue and interaction text

Read actual words, names, punctuation and any counts against a known original. The silhouette of a text panel is insufficient. A changed verb or item name can alter what the image appears to instruct, while neat-looking letterforms may conceal invented content.

If the source is illegible, mark it unresolved instead of completing the sentence from context. If a creator supplies the intended text separately, keep that distinction clear: it is additional evidence, not something recovered from the low-detail picture. This checklist does not promise that an image model will preserve that text after another attempt.

3. Crosshairs, reticles and selection markers

Check the marker's position, shape and relationship to the intended target. A small offset may be visually unobtrusive in an art reference but important in a picture presented as evidence of play. Do not silently recentre a marker to make a comparison look cleaner.

First distinguish a game HUD reticle from a highlight, emblem or prop in the scene. Then judge only the available frame. This review cannot establish aim accuracy, input response or whether a marker remains correctly aligned while a camera moves.

4. Menus, inventory slots and control prompts

Inspect item names, icons, selection states, slot boundaries and the association between a button prompt and its action. A plausible menu arrangement can still describe an action that was not selected. A newly invented icon is not a faithful version merely because it matches the art direction.

Compare the whole group as well as each item. If labels trade places, the text may remain individually familiar while the menu meaning changes. For submission, reject a claim of exact interface reproduction unless the original provides enough information to check those relationships.

5. Maps, navigation cues and counters

Look at marker positions, arrow directions, labels and counts. A miniature map can seem decorative when reduced, but a changed route or marker may give a different account of the game state. The same applies to ammunition and resource counters if they are present.

Keep unknowns explicit. Do not identify a location from an attractive redraw when its original label cannot be read. A creator using the image only for color mood can state that limited purpose; an image offered as a walkthrough needs a more demanding information check.

6. In-world lettering, insignia and character labels

Signs, patches, nameplates and equipment markings belong to the scene but can still carry authored meaning. Compare the actual text and the shape of important insignia where the source allows it. Do not assume that an invented symbol is acceptable simply because it is outside the HUD.

This is the category closest to our illustrated material. The signs look like designed visual forms, but the exact source strings are not established here. The defensible conclusion is that text fidelity remains unverified, rather than that the result reconstructed or destroyed a particular sentence.

Why text needs a separate acceptance standard

BFL's image-editing documentation describes text-and-image editing and includes text editing among the tasks. It does not provide a guarantee that incidental HUD content in our workflow is copied literally. Treating text as editable image content is different from verifying its semantic accuracy.

For an art-direction reference, you might accept lighting while rejecting the text area for use. For a tutorial screenshot, the same uncertainty may block the whole image. Make that use decision before submission. The difference is what the picture is being asked to prove, not whether the candidate is visually impressive.

Do not repair an unknown string by choosing something that sounds right. If you replace an interface element through another process, disclose that the final picture is a composition and verify the replacement independently. This is an editorial recommendation, not a claim that the current site provides an automatic HUD restoration feature.

A practical submission review

  1. Keep the untouched source beside the candidate and state the proposed use of the picture.
  2. Identify which of the six element groups are actually present. Mark absent groups not assessed.
  3. Compare literal content and placement before considering the attractiveness of the surrounding scene.
  4. Assign retained, changed or unresolved to each present element, with a short reason tied to the source.
  5. Reject unsupported gameplay or interface claims, or restrict the picture to a clearly labelled visual reference.
  6. Before sending, make sure the caption distinguishes a historical or generated example from a real gameplay observation.

We operate the linked site independently and are not affiliated with NVIDIA or Black Forest Labs. The illustrations are authorized site-owned historical samples, not official game screenshots. DLSS5NVIDIA / Free Passport Photo Maker

Free small tool · local processing

Free Passport Photo Maker — Printable 3×4 and 35×45 Photos

Create free printable 3×4 cm and 35×45 mm passport or document photos locally in your browser. Choose a verified format, align the guide and download a finished sheet without an account or credits.

Open the free local photo tool →

What a passport photo maker does

A passport or document photo maker prepares an image for a published physical size, resolution and head-position guide. This browser tool performs the crop and print layout locally, so the source photo stays on the device. It does not decide whether an immigration office, employer or other authority will accept the final image.

A repeatable local workflow

Choose the exact verified format first, then load a clear front-facing photo. The guide shows the target head height and headroom; adjust zoom and position until the crown and chin sit inside those lines. Select the output DPI, export one exact-size photo or lay out repeated copies on a printable sheet, and keep the original for any later correction.

Source quality still matters

The source should be sharp enough to print at the selected DPI, evenly lit and free from strong shadows, glare, sunglasses or cropped hair where the receiving authority prohibits them. A larger pixel count cannot repair a hidden eye, an obscured face or a background that fails the destination rule.

Check the receiving authority

The specification table records the printed dimensions, minimum DPI, background guidance and source date for each published format. Rules can change, and different authorities can interpret the same size differently. Confirm the current receiving authority instructions before you submit a photo or print sheet.

Why local processing matters

Local processing means the browser reads the selected file and draws the crop to a canvas on this device. The tool does not need an account, credits or a server upload to make the printable output. Clear the page or close the tab when finished if you are using a shared computer, and keep any downloaded copy in a location you control.

Troubleshoot before printing

If the export looks soft, start with a larger original and choose the minimum DPI required by the specification rather than enlarging a tiny screenshot. If the head does not fit the guide, adjust the crop before changing the output size. If a sheet is clipped by a printer, check the printer page size and disable “fit to page” so the physical dimensions remain exact.

Know the limits

This is a layout and crop utility, not an automatic compliance or biometric checker. It does not remove a background, change an expression, certify identity or submit a file to an authority. Those decisions belong to the person submitting the photo and to the authority that publishes the requirement.

Print at the documented size

For a physical sheet, use the paper size selected in the tool and print at 100 percent. Printer dialogs often add a “fit”, “shrink” or borderless option; those settings can change the millimetres even when the PNG itself is correct. Measure one printed tile with a ruler before making a full batch, especially when the receiving office has a strict size check.

Handle the downloaded file carefully

The tool is designed for a one-off local task: select a file, make the crop, download the output and clear the workspace. It does not require an account, does not send the source image to the enhancement API and does not retain a history of local exports. Treat the downloaded PNG like any other identity document and avoid leaving it in a public downloads folder.

Run the final checklist

A reliable final check is simple: confirm the selected format, confirm the printed millimetres, measure the exported tile, inspect the face and background at 100 percent, and compare the result with the authority’s current checklist. If any one of those answers is uncertain, keep the source and correct the crop before printing more copies. Save the exact specification and DPI alongside the file name so you can tell two similar exports apart later, especially when a family or team needs several formats. This avoids reprinting a whole sheet because a small setting was forgotten. For an important application, print one test tile first and have the applicant check the expression, hairline and background under normal light. Keep a note of the office or application type, because a visually similar document photo can still have a different size, head-height range or background rule. This final note makes a later recheck faster.

Published specification

Available verified formats:

  • Фото 3 × 4 см — 30 × 40 mm, minimum 600 DPI
  • Фото на паспорт РФ, 35 × 45 мм — 35 × 45 mm, minimum 300 DPI

How it works

  1. 1. Upload locally. Choose a JPG, PNG or WebP; the browser reads it without sending it to our server.
  2. 2. Align the guide. Position the crown and chin inside the published head-height and headroom lines.
  3. 3. Export. Download an exact-size PNG or a repeated print sheet with cut marks.

Before submitting

A correctly sized file is not a guarantee of acceptance. Check the receiving authority's current photo rules, expression requirements and background guidance.

DLSS5NVIDIA / DLSS 5 vs FSR 4

Source-led independent guide

DLSS 5 vs FSR 4

DLSS 5 and FSR 4 are vendor technologies in game-rendering pipelines. Compare the documented role, hardware scope and developer integration instead of promising a universal winner.

Do I use FSR or DLSS? Compare DLSS 5 vs FSR 4 by supported GPUs and game features, with NVIDIA and AMD sources and unverified claims clearly marked.

Source-checked answers

Last checked: 2026-10-23

These game features are separate from our independent DLSS 5-style conversion and neural-render redraw workflow and its DLSS5 Studio desktop handover.

Do I use FSR or DLSS?

Choose a feature that your game and GPU actually support. Check the game settings against NVIDIA’s DLSS and AMD’s FSR support information; a suite name alone is not a compatibility check. If both are available, compare the same scene and settings for the outcome you need. We have not verified a universal winner.

Sources: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/dlss-4-multi-frame-generation-out-now/https://gpuopen.com/amd-fsr-upscaling/ — checked 2026-10-23

How much better is DLSS 4.5 than DLSS 4?

NVIDIA describes a second-generation transformer for DLSS 4.5 Super Resolution, available for GeForce RTX GPUs. How much better it is for your game, GPU and settings is unverified (未核实) here: we have not run a matched benchmark and do not give a performance percentage.

Sources: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/dlss-4-5-dynamic-multi-frame-gen-6x-2nd-gen-transformer-super-res/ — checked 2026-10-23

Will AMD have something similar to DLSS 5?

Unverified (未核实): the AMD FSR source linked here is not evidence of an equivalent DLSS 5 neural-rendering product or a future release date. Check AMD’s own feature and hardware information. We do not treat upscaling or frame generation as proof of equivalent lighting and material rendering.

Sources: https://gpuopen.com/amd-fsr-upscaling/ — checked 2026-10-23

Read the DLSS 5, DLSS 4 and FSR 4 feature comparison · Choose a feature by goal, GPU series and checked game support

DLSS 5 source

NVIDIA documents 3D-guided neural rendering and its developer controls in the September 2026 launch article.

FSR 4 source

AMD’s FidelityFX Super Resolution page is the source for AMD’s current product description; individual game support still needs its own evidence.

Fair scope

A browser conversion on this site is independent and must not be labelled as either NVIDIA DLSS or AMD FSR.

Keep the vendor claims separate

NVIDIA and AMD publish different products, integration guidance and supported-game lists. This page links to each vendor’s own description and does not turn a marketing phrase into a cross-vendor score. DLSS 5 refers to NVIDIA’s documented neural-rendering stage; FSR 4 refers to AMD’s FidelityFX Super Resolution family. A browser conversion on this site belongs to neither runtime.

A fair test for a real project

Choose one source frame, one target size and one review checklist. Inspect silhouettes and repeated geometry first, then faces, text, thin edges and texture. Keep the original beside the output and record any prompt, preset or post-processing step. If the task is a game feature, use a game-specific support source; if it is an image task, run the same upload through the independent browser tool. This produces a useful decision without pretending that one universal winner exists.

Is the DLSS5NVIDIA converter DLSS 5?

No. It is an independent browser image workflow inspired by the visual goal; it does not install or emulate the NVIDIA runtime.

Which technology is better?

There is no universal answer without fixing a game, GPU, driver, resolution and image-quality test.

Is it true that DLSS 5 looks horrible?

There is no universal verdict: “looks horrible” is a visual judgment about a particular result. NVIDIA documents developer choices of model, structure, tone and where the effect is applied, plus an on/off toggle for players; those controls do not prove you will like the result. Compare the character and scene with the feature on and off; our independent style-conversion samples are not evidence of official runtime image quality. DLSS5NVIDIA / DLSS 5 vs DLSS 4.5

Source-led independent guide

DLSS 5 vs DLSS 4.5

These names describe different jobs in the rendering stack. DLSS 4.5 focuses on transformer-based super resolution and frame-generation modes; DLSS 5 adds a 3D-guided neural-rendering stage for lighting and materials.

Compare DLSS 5 vs DLSS 4.5: supported GPUs, RTX 50 series feature limits and what remains unverified, with dated NVIDIA sources.

Source-checked answers

Last checked: 2026-10-23

These game features are separate from our independent DLSS 5-style conversion and neural-render redraw workflow and its DLSS5 Studio desktop handover.

Is DLSS 4 only for RTX 50 series?

No. NVIDIA separates the features: Multi Frame Generation requires RTX 50; Frame Generation supports RTX 40 and RTX 50. The transformer updates for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction and DLAA are available across GeForce RTX GPUs, subject to game integration. Check the specific feature, not only the DLSS 4 label.

Sources: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/dlss-4-multi-frame-generation-out-now/ — checked 2026-10-23

How much better will DLSS 5 be?

NVIDIA describes DLSS 5 as 3D-guided neural rendering for lighting and materials. That is a different question from how many frames an upscaler produces. A general improvement amount is unverified (未核实) here; we have no matched game benchmark and do not turn NVIDIA’s demonstration into a universal quality or performance claim.

Sources: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/dlss-5-3d-guided-neural-rendering/ — checked 2026-10-23

Which GPUs are supported by DLSS 5?

The checked NVIDIA launch source confirms NBA 2K27 on all GeForce RTX 50 Series desktop and laptop GPUs, and separately on GeForce NOW. This answer’s local-PC scope is that named game and hardware family. Other local GPU/game combinations are unverified (未核实) here; a cloud service does not establish support on the client’s GPU.

Sources: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/dlss-5-3d-guided-neural-rendering/ — checked 2026-10-23

Read the DLSS 5, DLSS 4 and FSR 4 feature comparison · Choose a feature by goal, GPU series and checked game support

DLSS 5

NVIDIA describes a 3D-guided neural-rendering stage with structure, tone and semantic controls.

DLSS 4.5

NVIDIA describes a second-generation transformer model for Super Resolution and Dynamic Multi Frame Generation.

How to compare

Keep the same game, resolution and settings; do not treat a browser conversion result as an official in-game benchmark.

Compare roles before comparing numbers

DLSS 4.5 and DLSS 5 are not two presets that can be swapped in a generic image editor. DLSS 4.5 documentation focuses on transformer-based Super Resolution and Dynamic Multi Frame Generation. DLSS 5 documentation adds a 3D-guided neural-rendering stage for lighting and material response. A fair article therefore compares the documented role, the required game integration and the stated hardware scope before discussing output quality or frame rate.

A reproducible comparison protocol

Use the same game scene, resolution, graphics preset, driver branch and capture method. Record whether the measurement is an official NVIDIA figure, a local Studio run or an independent browser conversion. Do not combine an in-game frame-rate result with a still-image conversion and call the pair a benchmark. The only measured local video snapshot published here is 36 frames from a 3-second 720p clip in 87.4 seconds on one RTX 4090 reference machine; it is batch context, not a DLSS 5 versus DLSS 4.5 speed claim.
